## B. ROLE CONTRACT — DESTINATION vs ROUTE  (source: LORAMER_HANDOFF.md)
## ⛔ OPERATING DISCIPLINE — DESTINATION vs ROUTE (gate-level; read every session)
<!-- LORAMER_HANDOFF_OPERATING_DISCIPLINE_V1 -->
2026-06-23 FAILURE, named plainly: after correctly grounding in the repo, Claude converted ROUTE / sequencing decisions — its OWN job — into multiple-choice questions for Russ, and repeated it after being told to stop. Russ is NOT the coder or the plan-builder; offloading route decisions onto him is a FAILURE, not caution.

- DESTINATION vs ROUTE. Russ owns DESTINATION (what the app does/is; the governing law; genuine product forks the docs don't already answer). Claude owns ROUTE (how: sequencing, which platform/grain first, build order, whether to run a step the plan already specifies, blast-radius/safety). Claude DECIDES the route from the law + the plan, states a one-line reason, and proceeds — it NEVER asks Russ to choose the route.
- ASK RUSS ONLY FOR: (a) code/write approval — every code change, migration, deploy, before it runs; (b) a genuine product fork the governing law + the existing plan do NOT already answer. Everything else, Claude decides.
- BANNED ANTI-PATTERN: presenting an option-menu for a decision Claude should make. The ask-user-question tool is for product forks + preference elicitation, NOT for offloading sequencing Claude owns. "I don't care how, just do it right once" = Claude's cue to DECIDE and proceed, not to ask again.
- CONSULT THE PLAN BEFORE INVENTING: before proposing any "new" approach, check whether the plan ALREADY contains it (2026-06-23: a full Phase-4 breadth plan + LORAMER_COMPLETENESS_AUDIT_PLAN_V1 already existed; Claude began authoring a parallel one). If the plan has it, EXECUTE it and cite it; never freelance a duplicate.
- BLAST-RADIUS STATED, NOT ASSUMED: every proposed step names its blast radius, in order of safety — read-only investigation (always safe) → backend writer (isolated) → -next UI (preview-gated) → live-path (shared read-path / any live surface = STOP-and-confirm, never automatic). Live-path changes are allowed with graduated care. There is NO Meta review and no reviewer path — a shared-surface change STOP-and-confirms because of BLAST RADIUS (every client, every live surface), never a reviewer (the Meta App Review outcome that retired the reviewer path is owned by DECISIONS). Standing PRODUCTION obligations (not a freeze): the Meta data-deletion/deauth callback stays live (permanent Meta prod requirement), the Shopify install callback is a LIVE merchant path provisioning must not break, and Google Ads live snapshots stay quota-capped while Standard Access is pending (its live status owned by DECISIONS/QUEUE). A step touching a live/shared surface states "live-path" on its face and STOP-and-confirms.
- ONE THING AT A TIME: never stack a yes/no + a paste + a new question in one turn; when Russ answers a question, the NEXT turn does the WORK — it does not ask a follow-up question.
- OWN MISTAKES WITHOUT OFFLOADING: on error, acknowledge in one line, correct the route, and proceed — never convert recovery into more questions for Russ.

## C. GOVERNING LAW  (source: LORAMER_ESSENCE.md)
# ⛔ GOVERNING LAW — READ FIRST, OBEY ABSOLUTELY (no exceptions, no reinterpretation)
LoraMer captures EVERYTHING from EVERYWHERE and stores it FOREVER (until the customer cancels).
- EVERYTHING = every grain AND every dimension every platform exposes: account, campaign, ad_group/adset, ad, keyword, search_term, placement, device, geo, age/gender, hour/day, network, video, impression-share, all conversion/action types, product/variant, geo, and every other breakdown the API serves. If the API offers it, we capture it.
- EVERYWHERE = every connected platform: Google, Meta, Shopify, WooCommerce, GA — and any platform added later.
- FOREVER = forward capture appends daily and NOTHING is ever deleted or aged out; backfill reaches each platform's retention floor.
- FULL GRAIN, WITH HISTORY, IS THE DEFAULT. If the current code captures a thin slice (e.g. account-level only, or forward-only), that is INCOMPLETE CODE TO BE FINISHED — never a constraint to design around, and never labeled "future," "phase 4," "later," or "post-launch."
- The ONLY acceptable reason to not capture something is that the platform genuinely does not serve it (e.g. Google search terms beyond ~90d no longer exist to fetch). That is the ONLY exception. Filtering artifacts, missing params (campaign_id, time_increment), unbuilt writers, and "out of scope for this change" are NOT reasons — they are work to do.
- SEQUENCING is allowed ONLY as one-change-in-flight engineering discipline (each change reconciled, blast-radius-scoped, revert-ready). Sequencing NEVER means deferring, dropping, or relabeling any capture as out of scope. Everything is in scope, now, until Russ explicitly says otherwise.
- A fresh Claude that proposes a "persist the thin slice now, fuller grain later" plan has VIOLATED this law. Capture the full grain with history in the approved build.

## ⛔ ONE-BLOCK OUTPUT LAW — LORAMER_ONE_BLOCK_OUTPUT_V1 [LAW — RUSS, banked 2026-08-02, BROKEN 4× THE SAME DAY]
**EVERY substantive reply to Russ is ONE fenced code block. Nothing outside it. Ever.** Findings, code, guard
output, gate results, SHAs, sources, caveats, next steps — ALL INSIDE THE ONE BLOCK. No prose before it, no
prose after it, no "standing by" paragraph outside it, no sources line outside it, no second block.
WHY, and it is not style: **Russ reads and pastes on a phone.** Anything outside the block is content he
cannot carry — it is silently dropped the moment he moves the report. A reply split across three pastes is a
report he did not receive. ⛔ **IT WAS BANKED AND BROKEN ON THE VERY NEXT REPORT.** Per the RULE-HOME LAW,
prose is therefore not the fix and this entry is not the enforcer. **HONEST LIMIT: no repo guard can observe
Claude Code's chat output** — it never touches the filesystem, a commit or a build.
`tests/guards/one-block-output.guard.mjs` enforces the only mechanical thing there is: that this rule is
PRESENT AT THE TOP of the three docs the executor reads before acting (CLAUDE.md, here, RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS)
and reaches the generated digest. It guards PLACEMENT, never OBEDIENCE.

⛔ **AND THE SAME LAW HAS A SECOND HALF, BANKED 2026-08-04: TERSENESS IS A CORRECTNESS REQUIREMENT, NOT A STYLE PREFERENCE.** One block was always necessary and never sufficient — a single block full of padding fails for the same reason three blocks do. **THE COST, RECORDED SO IT IS NEVER MISTAKEN FOR TASTE: verbosity consumes APPROVAL BANDWIDTH, which is the scarcest resource on the 9/30 path — not compute, not quota, not typing.** Russ is the only human gate on every decision; every sentence he must read to find the decision is drawn from the one budget that cannot be topped up.
- **ANSWER, THEN STOP.** No editorialising. No summarising his own instruction back to him. He wrote it; he knows what it said.
- ⛔ **NEVER ASK FOR PERMISSION ALREADY GIVEN.** *"Say go and I'll send it"* is a wasted round trip when the go was in the message being answered. **Have the next paste READY IN THE SAME MESSAGE.** THE MOST-CORRECTED FAILURE OF 2026-08-03/04.
- ⛔ **ONE PASTE IN FLIGHT.** Never send a second while a report is outstanding. **VIOLATED THREE TIMES ON 2026-08-04, TWICE WHILE THIS VERY LAW WAS BEING WRITTEN.** If something else is ready, QUEUE it and say in one line what is queued.
- ⛔ **ANY RUNNABLE COMMAND GETS ITS OWN CODE BLOCK WITH ITS DESTINATION LABELLED** — Supabase SQL Editor, terminal, Vercel dashboard — **even if it is one word.** Prose containing a command is a DEFECT: it cannot be copied on a phone without hand-editing. Violated twice in a single exchange on 2026-08-04.
- **NO OPTION MENUS FOR DECISIONS CLAUDE OWNS.** Decide, state the decision and the reason in one line, move. Menus are for decisions that are genuinely his.
- **NO SCROLL-UP.** Anything he must DO is a plain bullet, not buried in a paragraph.

⛔ **THIS HALF HAS THE SAME HONEST LIMIT AS THE FIRST AND IT IS STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: NO GUARD CAN OBSERVE CHAT OUTPUT.** Per the RULE-HOME LAW, a rule broken repeatedly needs an ENFORCER and not another entry — and for chat there is none available, because the output never touches the filesystem, a commit or a build. `one-block-output.guard.mjs` guards PLACEMENT of this law in the three docs the executor reads; obedience has exactly one enforcer and it is Russ saying so again. **That is precisely why the cost is written down here: if the only enforcement is a human repeating himself, the law must at least tell him what it is costing him to do it.**

## ⛔ WHAT LORAMER IS — BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE, NOT MARKETING ANALYTICS [LAW — RUSS, banked 2026-07-31]
This is a SCOPE CORRECTION at law tier, and it governs the two laws above and every taxonomy below it.

**LoraMer is BUSINESS intelligence.** Given every grain a business will give her — advertising, store,
analytics, and whatever documents and context the owner uploads — **Lora reasons ACROSS ALL OF IT to answer any
question about how the business is actually performing and what to do about it.** Product prioritization. New
product ideas. Cost savings. Margin. Not "which campaign won" — *how is this business doing, and what should it
do next.* **And where the data cannot support an answer, she says so and names WHY** — which is the same
honesty the judgment half already demands, applied to a wider surface.

⛔ **THIS WIDENS THE EVAL TAXONOMY.** The 28-case golden set is marketing-analytics shaped — spend, ROAS,
conversions, breakdowns. A business-intelligence product is judged on questions that set never asks: which
products to cut, where margin is actually going, what to stock, what a cost line is doing to the bottom line.
The taxonomy has to grow to match the claim; a set that only asks marketing questions cannot certify a business
answer. Cross-ref ★EVAL-SET-EXPANSION — the expansion target is not just LARGER, it is a DIFFERENT SHAPE.

⛔ **AND IT WIDENS THE SEVERITY MODEL, which matters more.** A wrong ad recommendation is discovered in days
and costs a media test. **A wrong margin or inventory call moves what a business BUYS and STOCKS — higher
consequence, and far slower to discover.** Money goes out the door into physical goods on a purchasing cycle,
and the error surfaces a quarter later as dead stock or a cash-flow problem, by which point it is not
correctable by changing a bid. Severity is therefore NOT uniform across question classes, and any accuracy gate
that treats them as equal is mis-weighted. The 95% bar was set against marketing questions; it is not
automatically the right bar for a margin call.

## ⛔ THE JUDGMENT HALF OF THE GOVERNING LAW [LAW — 1-7 banked 2026-07-30, LAW 8 banked 2026-07-31, LAW 9 banked 2026-08-01]
The law above says capture EVERYTHING / EVERYWHERE / FOREVER. That is the SCOPE half. These EIGHT are the
JUDGMENT half — what "everything" means, when data counts as held, and what Lora owes when it is not.

**1. EVERYTHING MEANS EVERY INPUT THAT EXPLAINS PERFORMANCE, WHEREVER IT LIVES — not every field of the
reporting API.** Configuration (conversion window, attribution setting, whether conversion value includes
shipping/tax), change and activity history, negative-keyword lists, fee components, and off-platform
causation ARE DATA. ⛔ A family that has no `metrics_daily` row shape is NOT out of scope — it means THE
STORAGE SHAPE IS MISSING, not that the family is optional. Every past vendor-surface audit compared the
vendor's surface against "does this land in metrics_daily", which is a question that can never return a
config object, and so three whole families were structurally invisible to a process that ran repeatedly.

**2. UNWIRED IS MISSING.** Data captured but unreachable by Lora is data we DO NOT HAVE. The customer cannot
tell the difference, and neither can she. REFERENCE CASE: Shopify order-level taxes/shipping/discounts/tips
were captured 2026-07-01 (T1.5, into account `extra.money`) and on 2026-07-30 Lora told a user they were not
captured. Both facts were true at once. A capture flight is not done when the row lands; it is done when the
read path can reach it.

**3. PARTIAL DATA INVALIDATES A CONCLUSION — IT DOES NOT DEGRADE IT.** A recommendation built on 11 of 12
families is not 92% as good as one built on 12. The missing family is exactly where the counterargument
lives, and the confidence of the answer is unchanged by its absence — which is what makes it dangerous.
There is no partial credit in advice.

**4. THE PLATFORMS WILL NEVER RECOMMEND SPENDING LESS.** Google and Meta are paid when the customer spends;
their optimisation has a stake in the answer. Lora's only durable advantage is TOTAL DATA PLUS NO STAKE IN
THE ANSWER. That advantage is BINARY, not incremental: partial data with no stake is not a smaller edge, it
is no edge, because the recommendation can no longer be trusted over the platform's own.

**5. INSIDE THE WALL, "I DON'T KNOW" IS A BUG.** Outside a genuine vendor retention wall, Lora names the wall
and the date — that is a correct answer. INSIDE it, uncertainty is an INCIDENT: it means capture broke, and
it pages a human. Not a caveat, not a hedge — an alert. The distinction is mechanical, not editorial: which
side of the retention floor the window falls on.

**6. THE DANGEROUS STATE IS NOT "I DON'T KNOW" — IT IS A CONFIDENT ANSWER OVER AN UNCAPTURED WINDOW.**
An honest gap is recoverable; a confident answer over a hole is not, because nothing signals it. ⛔ THE
PREREQUISITE, and it is not optional: LORA MUST BE ABLE TO SEE HER OWN HOLES BEFORE SHE CAN BE TRUSTED TO
REPORT THEM. A coverage instrument nothing reads cannot make her hesitate.

**7. CLAIM-OF-NOVELTY GATE.** No finding, gap, or correction may be presented as NEW without first searching
the repo docs and the conversation history for it. ⛔ THIS IS NOT THE SESSION-START READ. Reading the entry
docs is INTAKE; this is a LOOKUP AT THE MOMENT OF CLAIMING, and only the second was ever missing. PRECEDENT,
2026-07-30: an entry was banked reading "A SECOND, TIGHTER GOOGLE WALL THAT NOTHING IN THIS REPO RECORDS"
when DECISIONS had recorded it months earlier, marked do-not-relitigate. The intake read had happened; the
lookup had not. A re-derived finding costs more than the thing it re-derives, because it also corrupts the
record.

**8. A NOTICED RISK IS NOT A CAVEAT. IT IS WORK.** If a risk, ambiguity, or "one thing worth knowing" is
noticed, it is RESOLVED before it is spoken — researched and fixed, or proven to be nothing. It is never handed
to Russ as a note to remember.
PRECEDENT, 2026-07-31: `entity_state_history` shipped with the observation that a zero-row table would be
indistinguishable from a broken writer. That was written into a summary AS A CAVEAT and the session moved to
wrap-up. Russ caught it without knowing any of the underlying detail, because it sounded wrong. He should not
have had to.
⛔ WHY IT RECURS: NAMING A RISK FEELS LIKE MANAGING IT. It is the same defect as a truncation warning that
fires nightly while nothing acts on it — Bath Fitter dropped its search-term tail for two months behind
exactly such a warning, and the warning was working perfectly the whole time.
THE TEST, BEFORE SPEAKING: is this resolvable from the data or the code RIGHT NOW? If yes — resolve it, do not
report it. If it genuinely cannot be resolved yet, it is NOT a caveat: it is THE NEXT ACTION, stated as an
action, with what unblocks it named.
COROLLARY (LORAMER_EMPTY_CARRIES_ITS_DENOMINATOR_V1): an empty result must carry its own denominator. No
capture pass, query or check reports zero without recording what it examined. "Check the logs before
concluding" is a human instruction, and human instructions are what fail.

**9. AN INSTRUCTION STATES THE GOAL AND THE CONSTRAINTS. IT DOES NOT STATE THE MECHANISM.** The conversation
layer reasons from REPORTS about the code; Claude Code reads the code. A report says what was EXAMINED, never
what was NOT, so the conversation layer's picture is ALWAYS A SUBSET — and writing an instruction in the voice
of someone holding the whole thing turns that subset into a FALSE PREMISE the executor must then spend the
flight disproving.
THE RULE: name what must be TRUE when the work is done, and what must not break. Where a mechanism is named,
mark it as a HYPOTHESIS TO VERIFY, never as a premise to build on. "Arm at every boundary where a Google error
is observed — establish what they are" is CORRECT. "Arm at withGoogleRetry, which every lane funnels through"
is a DEFECT, because it was not true.
PRECEDENT, 2026-07-31/08-01 — THREE false premises in ONE session, each costing a flight:
  · "withGoogleRetry, which every lane already funnels through" — 3 importers; the LIVE path bypasses it via
    withGaqlRetry + safeQuery; FORWARD calls the fetchers directly; and it did not classify quota AT ALL.
    There were FOUR boundaries.
  · "catchup's fillDays skip fires BEFORE the budget gate" — falsified; the gate at :282 is what CAUSES the
    skip at :594.
  · "the Google search-term floor is a vendor retention wall" — it is `DEFAULT_DAYS = 90` in our own backfill,
    and Google documents 37 months with NO search-term exception.
⛔ WHY IT RECURS: A MECHANISM STATED CONFIDENTLY READS AS RESEARCH ALREADY DONE, so it is built on rather than
checked. The executor then spends the flight disproving it instead of establishing the truth.
THE TELL, and it needs NO technical knowledge to spot: **if an instruction says HOW THE CODE WORKS, it is a
defect.** Whether the claim happens to be true is a SEPARATE question and not the point.
COROLLARY: a report opening "the briefed premise was false" is THIS LAW FAILING. Three in one session is a
signal, not a coincidence.
⛔ NOTE THE DIRECTION OF THIS ONE. Laws 7 and 8 bind the EXECUTOR; this one binds the INSTRUCTION. It is the
same failure all three share — treating something UNVERIFIED as SETTLED — and it is banked here rather than in
CLAUDE.md deliberately: CLAUDE.md gates what Claude Code will ACT ON, and a false mechanism is not refusable,
only checkable. The executor's obligation under this law is to VERIFY a named mechanism before building on it
and to SAY SO when it does not hold — never to assume the instruction did the research.


## ⛔ PRE-ACTION GATE (forcing function — output this line before ANY Claude Code paste or ANY UI proposal; a skipped line is a visible violation)
`in-flight: [what's running / clear] · blast-radius: [read-only|backend-writer|-next-only|live-path] · grid: [which card, or N/A non-UI] · high-stakes claim: [none | VERIFIED/DERIVED/UNVERIFIED + what]`
(The gate field is BLAST-RADIUS. Levels, safest→widest: read-only (always safe) → backend-writer (isolated) → -next-only (preview-gated) → live-path (shared read-path / any live surface = STOP-and-confirm, never automatic). Live-path is ALLOWED with graduated care. There is NO Meta review, no reviewer path, no reviewer-driven hold — blast radius on a shared surface is about EVERY client and EVERY live surface, never a reviewer (the Meta App Review outcome that retired the reviewer path is owned by DECISIONS, not restated here). Standing PRODUCTION obligations (not a freeze, not a review): the Meta data-deletion/deauth callback must stay live (permanent Meta prod requirement), the Shopify install callback is a LIVE merchant path provisioning must not break, and Google Ads live snapshots stay quota-capped while Standard Access is pending — the 15k/day Basic cap binds route decisions; its live status lives in DECISIONS/QUEUE, never here.)
High-stakes = any claim gating a destructive/rotate/delete action, a "this is a bug" diagnosis, or a blast-radius/live-path judgment. Rationale: the rules already exist; this converts the ones most often dropped under momentum (one-in-flight, blast-radius, grid-native, claim-confidence) into required visible output so a skip is caught in the moment, not after. Root cause: 2026-07-01 session — repeated rule-breaks despite the rules being present; the failure was compliance, not coverage. Do not relitigate.

## ⛔ THINGS RUSS SHOULD NEVER HAVE TO RE-STATE (settled non-negotiables — restate-to-prove each session)
- GOVERNING LAW (above): capture EVERYTHING / EVERYWHERE / FOREVER, full grain + history. A thin slice (account-only, forward-only) is UNFINISHED CODE, never a "phase-4 / later."
- VIDEO = ASSET **AND** METRIC, ALL MEANS ALL — the full video creative/asset layer AND the full video metric family (plays/ThruPlay/p25-100/avg-time/cost-per-thruplay), every grain, every platform.
- INVENTORY-FIRST sequencing — map all 5 platforms' full capture surface, THEN one master gap list + value-ordered build queue, THEN build. Never writer-by-writer ahead of the map.
- GRID-NATIVE: Everything analytical lives in the card-engine grid. No standalone data/analytics surface outside the card system — a new metric/breakdown is a card (or a card's detail view), never a floating panel. Building outside the grid is a STOP; state which card it is (or why it can't be one) before proposing any UI. Root cause: 2026-07-01 floating MoneySummary panel built outside the grid built the day prior.
- ASSET-COMBINATION CONVERSION ATTRIBUTION is the CORE capability — Lora names which creative COMBINATION (image/video + body + headline + CTA) drove which conversions BY TYPE, to the nickel, across Meta multi-asset + Google PMax incl. YouTube.
- 2027 WRITE DESTINATION is the WHY — Lora generates near-optimal ads (1–5% differentiation) + WRITES them to Meta/Google; the entire data foundation exists to enable this.
- PLATFORM-WIDE PLAYBOOK is a standing product goal (the whole-product operating playbook + the rote per-platform onboarding template).
- PROACTIVELY SURFACE non-coder-relevant risks/needs (token cliffs, scope gaps, cost/billing, reliability) the MOMENT they're visible — Russ is a non-coder; never wait to be asked.
- SEARCH-BEFORE-NEW — before presenting anything as a NEW finding/caveat/gap, search the docs + prior chats; if it's already decided, CITE the decision, do NOT reopen it.
- MULTI-SOURCE METRIC PROVENANCE: Any metric that can differ by source (ROAS, conversions, CPA, revenue, attribution) surfaces EVERY source's value, each labeled with its origin and basis. Never hide, blend, collapse, or silently pick one. The store is source-of-truth only for explicit store-truth questions; each platform's value stands on its own for platform questions; offline-uploaded sales enable a valid ROAS even without online purchase. Lora holds all sources at once, distinguishes them, and explains WHY they differ (web-researching the explanation when it helps). Every metric, every surface.
- VERIFICATION — REAL-PATH: a Gate-A proof traverses the REAL entry path (login / route / page) through EVERY gate/guard/middleware to the answer — isolated-function proofs are necessary, NEVER sufficient; on-device Gate-B on real data is the mandatory final backstop. (2026-07-11: two isolated-pass / live-fail misses. Full: DECISIONS VERIFICATION LAWS 1–3.)
- [LAW] LORAMER_REAL_INPUT_GATE_A_V1 — REAL INPUTS (alongside REAL-PATH above / DECISIONS LAWS 1 real-entry-path · 2 full-path recon · 3 whole-surface scoping). A Gate-A that HAND-SUPPLIES the input which makes the flag fire is a REHEARSAL, not a proof. Gate-A must DERIVE its inputs from the real resolvers and real DB rows for the case under test. Stubbing is permitted ONLY for state that cannot exist without a write (e.g. a not-yet-recorded failure streak), and every stubbed input must be NAMED as stubbed in the report. AND — any Gate-A for a user-visible flag must ENUMERATE EVERY surface that could display it and state, route by route, wired / not-applicable-and-why. PROVENANCE: T0 #2 slice 2 shipped a partial-total flag that passed 13/13 Gate-A while FAILING LIVE on the single most common real shape (healthy connection + window starting in-capture + stale tail) — the harness supplied coverage.state='trailing_gap'; the real getCoverageForWindows returns 'covered'. Three proofs passed; the phone showed the bug. And money + ga-overview were missed and surfaced one screenshot at a time. COROLLARY: when a defect appears on a surface a Gate-A declared green, the GATE-A IS THE FIRST THING TO FIX — before the code.
- LORAMER_CADENCE_V1 — HOW WE WORK (full spec: LORAMER_HANDOFF.md ## ⛔ LORAMER_CADENCE_V1). DELIBERATE SPEED / right-the-first-time: speed = NOT redoing work; verification ENABLES speed, never traded against it. COMMS: no commentary AFTER a code block (the block is LAST in the turn); exactly ONE code block per turn, newest in the message; ONE change in flight (no new paste while a report is outstanding — "logged, holding"); plain English + HALF THE WORDS for anything Russ reads/does; NO option-menus for a decision that is Claude's ROUTE. OWNERSHIP: Claude owns ROUTE (sequencing / build-order / blast-radius) and DECIDES + proceeds with a one-line reason — asks ONLY for (a) live-path/destructive/deploy/migration approval, (b) a real product fork the docs don't answer, (c) a real-world action only Russ can take. CADENCE: resume→freshness→restate→next→go, then Gate-A→ship→Gate-B auto-advancing down the queue; verify load-bearing claims via Claude Code BEFORE building (CHECK FIRST, don't ask what the repo answers); blast-radius one line per flight; live-path = graduated care, not a freeze and not a permission-gate for its own sake. KILL: narrating instead of executing · piecemeal plans (audit the WHOLE finish-line, then execute top-down BLOCKS-first) · over-cautious framing that gates low-stakes changes · post-code commentary. TIEBREAK between "PROACTIVELY SURFACE risks" (:24) and "no editorializing": SURFACE A RISK ONLY WHEN IT CHANGES RUSS'S NEXT ACTION. Otherwise it goes in the docs, not in his face.
- [LAW] VERIFY THE INSTRUMENT BEFORE TRUSTING THE MEASUREMENT. A test, scorer, benchmark, or proof is only evidence if the thing producing it has itself been verified THIS SESSION. A number from an unverified instrument is not a finding — it is a guess wearing a lab coat. This law would have prevented every correction of 2026-07-14/15.

- [LAW] THREE-SOURCE PRECONDITION (LORAMER_THREE_SOURCE_PRECONDITION_V1, RUSS, 2026-08-02) — **AN AMENDMENT TO WEB-FIRST DIAGNOSIS ABOVE, NOT A SECOND LAW SAYING THE SAME THING.** WEB-FIRST already names the three fields (HISTORY · WEB · REPO) and already widened to ANY build/fix/detector/schema change/diagnosis; this amendment changes WHEN the gate sits, WHO it binds, and WHERE the answer is written down. RUSS'S WORDS: "before ANY design, spec, or build instruction is written, all three must be done — (1) search all prior chats for the topic, (2) search the web as far as needed for accepted answers or existing published approaches, (3) have Claude Code search the repo, code and docs for prior discussion and prior work. Only once all three are done can any design or spec be written or anything built." THE THREE CHANGES: **(i) THE GATE MOVES EARLIER.** WEB-FIRST binds the PASTE that answers an instruction. This binds the INSTRUCTION ITSELF — the searches are a precondition of AUTHORING a design or spec, not of reporting one. A spec written from memory has already spent the budget by the time the executor's header is due. **(ii) IT BINDS THE AUTHOR, NOT ONLY THE EXECUTOR.** WEB-FIRST's enforcer is a header on Claude Code's paste; the thing being corrected all day was upstream of that paste. **(iii) THE ANSWER BECOMES AN ARTIFACT.** The header moves off the ephemeral paste and into the DECISIONS entry, where it is committed, greppable, and enforceable. THE REASON, plainly: the recurring failure is work being designed FROM MEMORY OR PATTERN rather than from sources. On 2026-08-02 every one of the day's four corrections — `synced_at` misread as a last-written stamp, "statement timeouts stopped 07-29" (a 50-group display cap, not a fact), the wrap-docs guard-count surprise, and "neither cursor advanced at 18:20Z" (read 2m54s too early, and the instruction it would have justified was to revert a WORKING fix) — traced to a source that was available and not consulted. THE ENFORCER (RULE-HOME LAW — a repeat-offense rule needs an enforcer, not another entry): `tests/guards/three-source-header.guard.mjs`, in `npm run guard`, requires the header on every DECIDED/DECISION/SHIPPED/LAW entry dated on or after 2026-08-02, all three legs present and non-empty; "NONE FOUND" is a valid answer, silence is not. ⛔ **THE LIMIT, STATED, NEVER IMPLIED AWAY** — inherited unchanged from WEB-FIRST because the amendment does not repair it: A GUARD CANNOT OBSERVE WHETHER A CHAT SEARCH OR A WEB SEARCH HAPPENED. Those occur before any code exists, in a transcript the guard cannot read and a browser it cannot see. The guard proves the ARTIFACT — three legs, non-empty — and NOTHING about whether a search occurred, was competent, or informed the design. The named residual failure is RUBBER-STAMPING, and it is documented prior art rather than our own worry: the ADR-enforcement literature warns that one rubber-stamp record "an agent later references as prior art propagates bad reasoning forward." A presence check cannot reach that; a human reading the legs can — which is why each leg must name WHAT WAS SEARCHED, not merely report a verdict.
- [LAW] FIX-WITH-GUARD — A FIX IS NOT DONE UNTIL A MECHANICAL CHECK FAILS WHEN IT REGRESSES. The guard ships in the SAME commit as the fix; a fix without its guard is not shipped. PROSE IN A DOC IS NOT A GUARD. A guard must be SEEN TO FAIL against the pre-fix code — a guard never observed failing is not a guard, it is a comment. Build it on the CODE (the thing that cannot lie about itself), never on a doc (a doc can be honest-but-false). Guard the CLASS, not today's instance: if the next writer/page/field can reintroduce the bug and the check still passes, it guards nothing. Where a pattern lives in N files, do not guard the convention — COLLAPSE IT TO ONE SOURCE and guard that (the settleRevenue / META_BREADTH_FORWARD shape): we fix files, we do not enforce rules. PROOF THIS IS NEEDED, 2026-07-15, both from this repo: (1) ESSENCE has said capture EVERYTHING/EVERYWHERE/FOREVER since day one, and 10 Meta breadth dimensions froze at their ship dates anyway, with two cursors sealing backfill_complete=13/13 over a permanent hole — nothing failed, the cron returned 200, and ~1,900 rows/client/day silently stopped existing. The law was written, present, and read every session; it changed nothing because nothing MECHANICAL enforced it. (2) The 2026-06-20 client-context fix was real, correct, and shipped — and regressed three weeks later at team/page.tsx:22 because the pattern lived in six files and no check could see the seventh. A law you cannot fail is a wish. If a mechanical guard is genuinely not achievable for a rule, SAY SO plainly rather than shipping a check that manufactures false confidence — an unenforceable guard is worse than none: it reads green exactly like sync_state read backfill_complete=13/13 while forward capture did not exist.

## ⛔ DETERMINISM OF JUDGMENT [LAW]
Given the same question over the same finite data, Lora must reach the same conclusion 100% of the time. Her answer may change ONLY when new or different information exists — and when it does, she must be able to say WHY it changed (attribution, not silent drift). This holds across model upgrades: Opus 4.8 → 4.9 → any successor must not change a conclusion.
MECHANISM (the model is never the thing that decides):
- NUMBERS: computed in code via ONE canonical settle. Lora REPORTS, never derives. (Fix #1 Part B is the first brick.)
- RECOMMENDATIONS: derived from deterministic, versioned, testable RULES. The model's job is to EXPLAIN the rule's output in English, never to originate the judgment.
- PROSE: not bitwise stable and does not need to be. If literal repeatability is ever required: hash (question + data fingerprint + memory state + prompt version + corpus version + model ID) → return the cached answer.
- MEMORY is INSIDE the exception: a stored correction IS new information. Requirement is ATTRIBUTION — Lora must cite which correction changed her answer.
- MODEL UPGRADES are gated by the eval. No model reaches users until the golden set passes with CONCLUSIONS unchanged. Precedent: Sonnet→Opus flipped B1 and D2 with identical code; the eval caught both.

[VERIFIED 2026-07-14, Anthropic docs — platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/model-ids-and-versions + /overview]
- claude-opus-4-8 is a PINNED SNAPSHOT, not an alias. From the 4.6 generation on, the dateless ID IS the snapshot; Anthropic does not update weights or config under an existing ID. New versions ship under new IDs. LoraMer is correctly pinned.
- CAVEAT: weights are fixed per ID, but SERVING INFRASTRUCTURE (request router, safety classifiers, sampling logic) can change under the same ID. So bitwise output stability is NOT guaranteed even on a pinned ID. This is why determinism must live in code, not in the model.
- CAVEAT: every model ID has its own deprecation/retirement schedule. Migration is eventually mandatory; the eval gate is what makes it safe.
- CAVEAT: Opus 4.8 uses adaptive thinking with effort defaulting to HIGH on all surfaces — a live variance source today.

## ⛔ GROUNDED RECOMMENDATIONS / THE CORPUS [LAW]
- Lora's recommendations are grounded in a FROZEN, VERSIONED best-practice corpus — NEVER a live web search. Live search is a determinism bomb: same data, different day, different answer, no new information from the user. A corpus VERSION BUMP is new information: dated, attributable, eval-gated, roll-back-able.
- The corpus feeds the RULES, not the prose. Every recommendation CITES its source (corpus / the user's own correction / the platform's own doc). "Argue with her" is the product: she shows her sources, the user can dispute them. Same moat as multi-source metric provenance — explaining WHY, applied to judgment.
- POSITIONING (true, defensible): Google's and Meta's recommendation engines are structurally conflicted — their revenue IS the advertiser's spend. LoraMer's revenue is a subscription. Frame as INCENTIVE ASYMMETRY, never "they lie" — some of their advice is good, and overclaiming hands a skeptic an easy win.
- HONESTY BOUND: much of marketing canon is contested (brand vs. performance, attribution, incrementality). Never claim Lora knows THE truth. The claim is that she shows her sources and can be argued with.
- RISK FLAGGED, UNRESOLVED: ingesting third-party copyrighted marketing material into a corpus whose output is resold is real IP exposure, distinct from a human reading it. Public-domain / licensed / primary sources / Russ's own writing are clean. NOT legal advice — needs a real lawyer before the corpus scales.

## ⛔ "MAKE LORA YOUR OWN" — WHAT THE PROMISE CAN AND CANNOT CASH [LAW]
CAN: her name/voice/tone; the org's definitions (net sales, value model, ROAS basis); their documents; their retained corrections; their guardrails. All config, all real.
CANNOT: "a different mind" (weights are shared and rented); "she knows everything about us" (the librarian SELECTS — omission is the mechanism, not a bug); "exclusively yours" (direct tension with the cross-agency LoraMer tier — a POSITIONING FORK, unresolved: exclusive-yours vs compounding-across-agencies cannot both be headlined); "you own her" (implies portability/export — a moat hole if yes, marketing if no; decide knowingly).
COST LAW: per-org memory grows the briefing packet forever → input tokens rise per turn, per customer, permanently. Cost scales with ENGAGEMENT; best customers cost most. Must be budgeted before memory ships.
COPY GUARD: "she learns YOUR WAY OF WORKING" is true and defensible. "She BECOMES yours" is the check that bounces.

## HOMEPAGE / BOTTOM-OF-PAGE MESSAGE (banked for the two-door homepage item)
"The model is rented. The memory isn't." Every tool in the category runs on the same frontier AI anyone can rent — that's the starting line, not an edge. LoraMer's edge is what it KEEPS: every platform captured at full grain from the day you connect. So when Shopify and GA disagree, Lora shows BOTH, labeled by source, and explains why — the question every other tool hides from. A competitor can rent the same model tomorrow. They can't rent your history.
GUARDS: (a) "from the day you connect" is load-bearing — backfill is bounded by platform retention; never let it be edited into "all your history." (b) The cross-agency brain is ANONYMIZED PATTERNS, not data — any line implying Lora learns across agencies must read that way, or it reads as "your client data feeds your competitor."

If a change makes Lora more confident but not more provable, it is wrong.

Recovery is a READ (GET /api/conversations); it NEVER re-POSTs /api/chat, because a silent retry doubles the spend on a turn that most likely already succeeded. - [SHIPPED 2026-07-27] **LORAMER_SHOPIFY_DEPTH_NOTNULL_FIX_V1 — the Shopify depth write had been 23502-ing every night since 2026-07-19, and the account row's freshness hid it.** ROOT CAUSE, and it is a platform behaviour worth never relearning: **PostgREST builds ONE column list from the UNION of keys across a bulk payload, and any object missing a key that a SIBLING object supplies is sent as an explicit NULL — NOT the column DEFAULT.** `buildShopifyDepthRows` omitted `conversions` on product_type / product_vendor (intelligence-types.ts:418-419 — those two capture shapes carry `{value, netRevenue}` and no unit count, unlike product_tag which has `units`) while every sibling family set it, so Postgres rejected the WHOLE statement: `null value in column "conversions" of relation "metrics_daily" violates not-null constraint`. MEASURED IN PROD off Vercel's 7-day error-cluster table: 32 rejections naming `conversions`, plus 16 naming `spend` on days whose payload also carried a discount/abandoned row that DID set spend — four stores (Foam OH, Influential Drones, The Escential Group, Cozy Foam Factory), thirteen order-days with real money and no depth row beneath them. IT WAS INVISIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION: cron/sync writes the account row and the depth rows as TWO SEPARATE upserts (:319 and :335), the depth one inside its own try/catch that logs and continues — so the account row landed, connection health stayed green, sync_state advanced, cron returned 200, and `cron_runs.error_count` read 23 against 6 errored connections with nobody reading the difference. THE FIX, two files: (1) `conversions: 0` on the two rows — explicit 0, because there is genuinely no count in scope and the KEY'S PRESENCE is the load-bearing part; (2) `normalizeMetricsRows` union-fills any NOT-NULL numeric that a sibling row supplies. **UNION-SCOPED ON PURPOSE — never "always set all six":** filling a column absent from the ENTIRE payload would ADD it to the column list, and on a merge-duplicates upsert that turns a column the writer deliberately left untouched into one overwritten with 0 on every conflict. THE GUARD (same commit, FIX-WITH-GUARD): `tests/guards/metrics-payload-uniformity.guard.mjs`, wired into `npm run guard`. It DERIVES payload shapes BY EXECUTING the five real builders (a text scan cannot see which rows land in the SAME statement), reads the NOT-NULL set from information_schema via a committed snapshot, exempts nullable columns BY NULLABILITY not by name, and covers forward + backfill shapes on all five platforms. PROVEN RED THEN GREEN: pre-fix builder + pre-fix normalize → exit 1, 16 violations; post-fix builder + pre-fix normalize → exit 1, 12 (the guard independently confirming file 1 alone was insufficient); both post-fix → exit 0. EQUIVALENCE PROVEN BEFORE WIDENING THE BLAST RADIUS: the two normalizers are byte-identical on every payload that writes today — 5/8 executed platform payloads identical, the 3 that differ are exactly the 3 that currently throw, and a 60,000-payload property run returned 0 writing-payloads changed. **WOOCOMMERCE CARRIED THE IDENTICAL DEFECT** (spend/impressions/clicks/conversion_value on 3 of 13 rows, and its single-statement upsert would have lost the ACCOUNT row too) — closed by the same normalize change with zero edits to the Woo builder; it had simply never fired because no Woo store has had an order since the writer shipped. | LORAMER_SHOPIFY_DEPTH_NOTNULL_FIX_V1, 2026-07-27 | do not relitigate.

- [LAW COLLISION 2026-07-28 — RESOLVED, and written down precisely so nobody "simplifies" it back to a boolean] **FAIL-CLOSED EVERYWHERE WOULD HAVE BROKEN A DO-NOT-RELITIGATE LAW, AND THE SPLIT IS WHAT LETS BOTH STAND.** The obvious fix — error → `paused:true` — is correct for the capture lanes and WRONG for the answer path, because `readGoogleQuotaPause` has two kinds of caller: cron/drain and cron/catchup turn the answer into "do I spend Google quota" (a false hold costs one lap, retried in ~10 min, self-healing), while /api/intelligence turns it into a USER-FACING CLAIM — buildGoogleQuotaLines renders "⛔ GOOGLE PLATFORM API QUOTA EXHAUSTED … SAY THIS OUT LOUD" plus an instruction not to offer a retry. Under fail-closed with a null row that block renders with `until` unset, so Lora would tell a user the quota is exhausted until "the next daily reset" when the only thing that happened is a Supabase blip and live Google data is fine. That directly violates **FAIL-PARTIAL READ-PATH LAW** (064dd54, 2026-07-11: read-path endpoints fail PARTIAL + LOUD, never fail-closed-silent) and re-creates the exact incident **VERIFICATION LAW 1** was written from ("Lora: /api/intelligence fail-closed on a network blip"). Sources: web.dev/articles/speedy-css-tip-animated-gradient-text · theadminbar.com/how-to-create-animated-background-gradient-text-with-css · amitmerchant.com/animated-gradient-effect-in-css · sitepoint.com/css-animate-text-gradients-patterns · dev.to/ibelick animated text gradient. · REPO: read the rule and the keyframes together rather than separately — which is what exposed it, because the defect exists only in the INTERACTION of `background-size: 400%`, `background-repeat: no-repeat` and the keyframe range. THE MECHANISM, DERIVED:** for `background-position: P%` with `background-size: 400%` on a box of width W, the image is placed at `offset = (W − 4W) × P = −3W × P`, and with `background-repeat: no-repeat` the image covers the box ONLY while `offset ≤ 0 AND offset + 4W ≥ W`, i.e. **`0% ≤ P ≤ 100%`**. The keyframes ran **100% → −100%**. At P = −100% the offset is **+3W** — the image sits ENTIRELY TO THE RIGHT of the box, the box has NO background, `background-clip: text` clips nothing, and with `-webkit-text-fill-color: transparent` **the glyphs render FULLY TRANSPARENT.** Half of every cycle was spent walking the gradient off the text. That is the vanish, and it is the position spec, not a repaint bug. FIXED: travel is now **100% → 0%**, inside the covered range at every frame, so some legible colour is on every glyph at every moment and the line CANNOT disappear. Because the gradient's outer thirds are flat `--muted`, both endpoints render as uniform muted text — it parks at neither end looking broken, which is what "calm, not broken" requires. TIMING: **6s, `ease-in-out`, `alternate`** (was 2.4s linear). 6s per traversal — a 12s round trip — because at 2.4s the highlight crossed ~25 times a minute and read as a blink; `ease-in-out` because the highlight must slow where the reversal happens; and **`alternate` is what removes the SNAP** — a one-way animation must jump from its end value back to its start on every iteration, and that discontinuity is one no easing can hide. ⛔ **DEFECT 1 — THE RESERVE WAS ON THE WRONG SIDE, AND `min-height` IS THE REASON.** A min-height says how TALL a block is and says NOTHING about which side the slack falls on; the surrounding flex chain decided, and it decided BOTTOM — mark and line hard against the composer with the emptiness above. absolutely positioned it costs the same 46px as `padding-right` but only on the LAST line, because text wraps above it. ⛔ **ITS OFFSETS COME FROM `--composer-pad-x` / `--composer-pad-b` PUBLISHED BY THE COMPOSER, NOT FROM A LITERAL — the page variant adds `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` and the panel does not, so one hard-coded `bottom` would be wrong on one of the two surfaces and would look right on whichever was tested.** **AUTO-GROW is native where it exists** (`@supports (field-sizing: content)`) **and a gated JS effect where it does not**, both keyed off the SAME query (`CSS.supports('field-sizing','content')`) so exactly one mechanism is ever live. ⛔ **`height='auto'` BEFORE READING `scrollHeight` IS THE WHOLE TRICK: scrollHeight on an element already sized to its content returns that size, so without the reset the field RATCHETS UP and never shrinks when cleared.** ⛔ **THE CAP IS A DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM THE BRIEF AND IT IS STATED, NOT SLIPPED IN: the instruction said "~40% of viewport", but the SHIPPED 120px is STRICTER than 40% of any phone (40vh of an 844px iPhone is ~338px), so raising it would have made the brief's own stated problem — a long paste eating the thread — WORSE while appearing to comply.** `max-height: min(40vh, 120px)` keeps both: 120px binds on a phone, 40vh takes over only on a viewport short enough that 120px would itself be 40%. **vh, NOT dvh — this stylesheet bans dvh outright** (its header records that on iOS dvh resolves to the LARGE viewport), and the cost is stated: that term is computed against the larger viewport, and it does not bind on a phone anyway. **font-size 16px was ALREADY correct and was NOT changed** (LORAMER_NEXT_CHAT_INPUT_16PX_V1, measured 1.1431818x) — reported as already-done rather than re-shipped as new work. GUARDED by `tests/guards/chat-composer-and-bleed.guard.mjs`, six legs, **SEEN RED against pre-fix HEAD 41ff41b in a scratch tree under `LORAMER_GUARD_ROOT` — 6 findings — then GREEN.** ⛔ **ITS LIMIT IS WRITTEN ON ITS FACE AND MUST NOT BE OVER-READ: ★CHAT-RENDER-MEASUREMENT-MISSING IS OPEN, SO IT ASSERTS CSS DECLARATIONS AND NOT ONE PIXEL.** It cannot see that the composer is full width, that the button paints inside the field, that the text is wider, or that the field grows and shrinks — all four are LAYOUT claims and belong to Gate-B on device. | src/components/redesign/lora-thread.module.css, src/components/redesign/LoraThread.tsx, tests/guards/chat-composer-and-bleed.guard.mjs | do not relitigate.

No Stripe columns/tables/env anywhere — greenfield"* — and `:11` records that tier ENFORCEMENT is likewise absent. **So the dependency is real AND it is itself unbanked**; a one-click expensive button turns that from theoretical to urgent. ⚠ **NAMED FOR RUSS'S DAUGHTER — a trademark glance is owed before it ships on a paying-customer surface**, and that is a five-minute check that gets much more expensive after launch. **RANKED AFTER THE 9/30 ARC.** src: 2026-08-03 Russ. open [LC]

- ★FLEET-SPEND-OMITS-INTELLIGENCE-LANE — ⛔ **NEW 2026-08-04, FOUND WHILE BUILDING THE FLEET GOVERNOR, AND IT UNDER-COUNTS IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION.** `readGoogleSpendToday()` attributes spend by `cron_runs.mode` — forward, catchup, drain — and **`/api/intelligence` writes NO `cron_runs` ROW AT ALL.** It makes live Google Ads calls on user page loads, so every dashboard view spends operations that are invisible to every budget decision in the system. ⇒ **FLEET SPEND IS UNDER-REPORTED BY WHATEVER THE INTELLIGENCE LANE USED, WHICH MEANS THE GOVERNOR CAN AUTHORISE A PUBLISH THAT BREACHES THE CAP.** ⚠ **AND THE REST IS AN ESTIMATE, NOT A MEASUREMENT:** ops are modelled as `units × GAQL_REQUESTS_PER_CONNECTION_DAY (67)`, forward/drain billed per connection-day and catchup per gap-day. - ★NUMBER-ACCURACY-IS-100-NOT-95 — ⛔ **NEW 2026-08-04. RANK INSIDE THE 9/30 ARC. THE FOUNDER'S OWN VERDICT ON THE FIRST WORKING PREVIEW SESSION: THE ANSWERS ARE EXCELLENT AND HE HAS NO CONFIDENCE THEY ARE TRUE.** That sentence is the product problem, and it splits in two — **and the split is the entire point of this entry.** ⛔ **PROSE REASONING IS A MODEL PROBLEM.** It is what the eval measures, it degrades gracefully, and **95% is a legitimate target** because the remaining 5% is judgement. ⛔ **A NUMBER IS NOT A MODEL PROBLEM. IT COMES FROM SQL. A WRONG NUMBER IS A QUERY DEFECT AND ITS TARGET IS 100%** — mechanical, closeable to zero, and there is no principled reason to accept any of it. **CONFLATING THEM IS ACTIVELY HARMFUL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: the eval scores the MODEL for a MECHANICAL failure it did not cause, and the mechanical class — the one that can actually be driven to zero — hides inside a 95% target that says it is fine.** **THE EVIDENCE IS ONE DAY'S WORK, 2026-08-04, AND EVERY ITEM PRODUCED A CONFIDENT, SOURCED, WRONG NUMBER WITH NO MODEL FAILURE ANYWHERE:** (1) ratios computed on refused denominators — **119,375 of 119,375 stamped rows**, every one carrying a ROAS/CPA/CPC built on a metric the vendor refused; (2) **~1.5M pre-fix rows** holding a refused metric as an unstamped `0`; (3) a read-path defence keyed on the row's own stamp would have worked on the JS paging path and **silently not worked on the SQL GROUP BY fast path**, which is the one that runs for every large breakdown; (4) derived-time families written where undeclared — **11 tuples Lora could not read at all**; (5) the yield-rank join matching **0 of 358** and printing it as data. ⇒ **FIVE DISTINCT MECHANICAL PATHS TO A WRONG NUMBER, FOUND IN A SINGLE DAY, NONE OF THEM THE MODEL.** ⛔ **AND THE MOST DANGEROUS PROPERTY THEY SHARE: every one is INVISIBLE TO THE READER. A refused metric rendered as 0 looks exactly like a real 0; a join matching nothing looks exactly like a true zero.** These do not announce themselves the way a bad sentence does. **CROSS-LINK [[★SEMANTIC-LAYER]] — it serves BOTH halves and is not restated here (LORAMER_DOCS_SINGLE_OWNER_V1):** structurally correct numbers for this item, and for the prose half its published finding that the failure mode shifts from confident-wrong to REFUSAL, which is the 34.5% adversarial/calibration slice. ⚠ **THE HONEST LIMIT: 100% is the target for the MECHANICAL class only.** It does not promise a correct answer — a perfectly correct number can still be the wrong number to have quoted, and that failure stays in the prose half where the eval belongs. src: 2026-08-04 preview session. open [LC]
- ★NUMBER-PROVENANCE-SPOT-CHECKABLE — ⛔ **NEW 2026-08-04. THE CONFIDENCE INSTRUMENT, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT FROM THE ACCURACY ONE — RANK IT AS SUCH.** ⛔ **A HIGHER SCORE DOES NOT PRODUCE TRUST; A CHECKABLE NUMBER DOES.** [[★NUMBER-ACCURACY-IS-100-NOT-95]] raises the accuracy; this makes any single figure VERIFIABLE IN SECONDS, so trust stops being all-or-nothing about a whole answer. **Today the founder's only options are believe the entire response or believe none of it — and he chose none, on answers that were in fact good.** THE REQUIREMENT: every figure Lora states must be traceable to the query that produced it, carrying **the grain · the date window · the source platform · whether the value is CAPTURED or COMPUTED · and whether any input metric was REFUSED at that grain**. ⛔ **IT MUST WORK ON THE SQL `GROUP BY` FAST PATH, NOT ONLY THE JS PAGING PATH.** `query_breakdown_agg` returns SUMS ONLY — `extra` never crosses the wire — so a provenance mechanism built on the row's own stamp would work on one path and silently not the other. **That is the narrow-green shape this repo keeps finding, and the read-path fix hit exactly it on 2026-08-04**; it is written here so the next builder does not rediscover it. ⇒ **IT IS ALSO THE EVAL INSTRUMENT, and this is the argument for building it early: a wrong number WITH provenance is DIAGNOSABLE — you can see which query, which grain, which window produced it — while a wrong number without it is only a SCORE.** Provenance turns every eval failure into a bug report instead of a percentage. ⚠ **UX SHAPE IS UNDECIDED AND IS RUSS'S CALL — inline, hover, or a drawer. Deliberately NOT decided here; the requirement is that the data reaches the surface, not how it is drawn.** src: 2026-08-04 preview session. open [LC]
- ★SEMANTIC-LAYER — ⛔ **NEW 2026-08-03. THIS IS THE 95% EVAL PATH, NOT A NICE-TO-HAVE. RANK IT INSIDE THE 9/30 ARC, AHEAD OF [[★EVAL-SET-EXPANSION]], because it changes WHAT THE EVAL MEASURES rather than how much of it there is.** **MEASURED AND PUBLISHED, 2026:** grounding the same questions in a semantic layer instead of raw text-to-SQL moved **Claude Sonnet 4.6 from 90.0% → 98.2%** and **GPT-5.3-Codex from 84.1% → 100%** (dbt Labs, 2026-04-07, `docs.getdbt.com/blog/semantic-layer-vs-text-to-sql-2026`); a separate paper reports **94.15% execution accuracy on Spider2-snow** via a semantic-layer-mediated agent. ⛔ **BUT THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE FAILURE MODE, NOT THE RATE: semantic-layer failures are REFUSALS ("I can't answer that"); text-to-SQL failures are CONFIDENT WRONG NUMBERS.** That is precisely our acknowledge-then-fabricate defect and the 34.5% adversarial/calibration slice — **and the literature says it is ARCHITECTURAL, not a prompting problem**, which means no amount of prompt work closes it. ⇒ **A wrong margin call is discovered a quarter later as dead stock (ESSENCE's severity law); a refusal is discovered immediately. Trading confident-wrong for honest-refusal is the whole product thesis, stated as an architecture rather than as an instruction.** **WE ALREADY HOLD A PARTIAL SEMANTIC LAYER — `src/lib/breakdown-registry.ts`.** The work is PROMOTING it from *"this breakdown exists at these grains"* to **CERTIFIED METRIC DEFINITIONS**: net sales, ROAS, blended vs platform-reported, which denominators are legal, and the refused-metric rules. ⛔ **IT FOLDS IN [[★UNIVERSE-REFUSED-METRIC-READ-PATH]] RATHER THAN COMPETING WITH IT** — *"never build a ratio on a refused denominator"* is EXACTLY a certified-metric rule, and that item's own honest limit is that the rule currently lives in prose while `metrics-query.ts` still hands back a divisible 0. **Prose is not a guard (banked law); a certified metric layer is where that rule becomes mechanical.** ⚠ **PRIOR ART IN THIS REPO, cite rather than re-derive: DECISIONS 2026-07-14 already banked that our approach IS the semantic-layer pattern the field converged on (dbt/MetricFlow, Snowflake Cortex Analyst), and the OPEN LAW QUESTION beside it — a semantic layer buys determinism with COVERAGE, since it can only answer what is modelled — is still open and is the real design tension here.** src: 2026-08-03. open [LC]

This is a false claim about OUR OWN RECORDS** — the one place we are supposed to be able to trust without checking — and it survived a full day of being cited because citing is cheaper than searching. **CHEAP MITIGATION, not built: a guard that extracts every `[[★TOKEN]]` from QUEUE/DECISIONS/CONTINUE_HERE and fails on any that matches no entry header.** That is mechanically decidable, unlike most of law 9. src: Russ 2026-08-02, banked 2026-08-03. open [LC]
- ★USAGE-CAP-ABSENT — ⛔ **NEW TO THE QUEUE 2026-08-03. OPEN SINCE 2026-07-20 AND NEVER BANKED. THERE IS NO USAGE CAP ANYWHERE IN THE PRODUCT.** Every member has effectively unlimited Opus against Russ's Anthropic account, and **at $0 balance Lora does not degrade — she BLANKS.** ⛔ **VERIFIED FROM SOURCE RATHER THAN ASSERTED, and the source says it plainly: `STRIPE_BILLING_PLAN.md:12` — "anthropic_spend_log exists (per-call cost log, NOT A QUOTA). No Stripe columns/tables/env anywhere — greenfield"; `:11` — tier ENFORCEMENT is absent (`user_profiles.tier` exists as a column with nothing reading it).** So the instrument that would tell us the number EXISTS and is written by `src/lib/spend-logger.ts`, and nothing acts on it. **MINIMUM VIABLE MITIGATION IS A BALANCE ALARM, NOT FULL BILLING** — a threshold on the Anthropic account plus a Supabase billing alert, an afternoon of work, and it converts a silent product-wide outage into an email. ⛔ **FULL METERING IS THE BIGGER JOB AND IT MUST NOT BLOCK THE ALARM.** Do not let "we need proper billing" postpone the cheap thing that prevents the outage. ⛔ **HARD DEPENDENCY OF [[★MERIDA]], CROSS-LINKED BOTH WAYS: a one-click "analyse everything" button against an uncapped account is the runaway-cost class** — the cost is loop length, one user can press it repeatedly, and nothing anywhere stops them. ⚠ **SAME FAILURE SHAPE AS [[★MCP-BASELINE-HEAD-TO-HEAD]], banked the same day: Claude flagged this all of 2026-08-03 as a known dependency, as though it were tracked. It was not.** Two items in one day cited as banked while unbanked is not coincidence, it is a hole in how work gets from a strategy chat into the record. ⛔ **CORRECTION BANKED 2026-08-04 — I SENT RUSS LOOKING FOR A FEATURE THAT DOES NOT EXIST, TWICE.** This entry previously recommended "a Supabase billing alert threshold" as the cheap mitigation. **THERE IS NO SUCH FEATURE.** Supabase's own cost-control documentation states the Spend Cap **does not allow fine-grained control such as budgets per usage item or notifications at a cost threshold**. Russ went looking twice and found nothing, because there was nothing to find. **WHAT ACTUALLY EXISTS, so nobody hunts again:** (1) **the Spend Cap is BINARY** — either it blocks everything over the plan quota or it permits full usage-based billing; there is no threshold, no per-item budget, no notification. **It is currently OFF, deliberately** — turning it ON would mean the product stops rather than overspends, which is a product decision, not a monitoring one. (2) ⛔ **EVEN WITH THE SPEND CAP ON, ADD-ONS INCLUDING EXTRA COMPUTE ARE ALWAYS BILLED — it would NOT have capped tonight's XL upgrade.** Anyone reaching for the Spend Cap to control compute cost is reaching for the wrong lever. (3) **The ONLY monitoring is the org usage page, read manually, refreshing roughly hourly** — so there is no push signal at all, only a page someone remembers to open. ⛔ **AND THE REAL RISK IS NOT A SURPRISE BILL — IT IS THAT PRO CAN GO READ-ONLY.** Hitting the disk-expansion limit (**4 modifications per rolling 24 hours**) can put the project into a read-only state, which is an OUTAGE, not an invoice. ⇒ **THAT IS WHY THE 40 GB DISK FLOOR IN `scripts/partition-backfill.mjs` IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT A NICETY**, and why it refuses "one more batch": the platform's own safety net cannot be relied on, the modification window can be exhausted exactly when it is needed, and the failure mode is the database going read-only rather than a line item on a bill. ⚠ **FILED AS A [[LORAMER_ESSENCE_LAW_9_V1]] PRECEDENT on [[★FLIGHT-REPORT-NAMES-ASSERTED-MECHANISMS]] — the SIXTH — and it is the SAME SHAPE as the Google Ads API Center screen that does not exist: a mechanism asserted without a source, which cost a human two trips to look for something that was never there.** The pattern is now unmistakable: when I name a UI affordance I have not seen, I should say I have not seen it. src: 2026-07-20, banked 2026-08-03; correction 2026-08-04. open [LC]
- ★GUARD-BREAK-AND-RESTORE-IS-UNSAFE — ⛔ **NEW 2026-08-03, FROM A LIVE NEAR-MISS RUSS CAUGHT BY REJECTING THE TOOL CALL.** A red-proof that BREAKS a file and then RESTORES it is unsafe by construction: if the process dies, is killed, or the call is rejected between the two steps, **the file stays broken and the guard's own green becomes a lie about a tree that no longer exists.** ⛔ **THE INCIDENT:** while adding leg (e) to `universe-derived-time.guard.mjs` I authored a single call that (1) shortened `WRITER_METRICS` in `scripts/google-ads-capture-universe.mjs`, (2) stripped `servesMetrics` from **`docs/google-ads-capture-universe.json` — the file that had just cost 463 vendor requests to measure and is NOT cheaply recoverable** — and (3) restored both afterwards. Russ rejected the call. **It happened to land BEFORE the break (verified by re-reading the file, not by assuming), so nothing was damaged** — but the window was real and the artifact was the thing in it. ⚠ **AND IT CARRIED A `git checkout scripts/...` FALLBACK, which would have discarded uncommitted flight work** — a second, independent way for the same call to destroy something. **THE RULE, applied in this commit and to be applied to the existing legs later:** a break-and-restore leg operates on a **COPY** — build a throwaway tree, point `LORAMER_GUARD_ROOT` at it, mutate THAT — so interruption at any point leaves the real files byte-identical. Proven in this commit: four red proofs ran and the real artifact/generator/writer md5s were identical before and after. ⛔ **NEVER a `git checkout` inside a proof** — it cannot distinguish the mutation from real work. **NOT SWEPT TONIGHT, deliberately:** the existing legs in `universe-entity-axis`, `universe-artifact-slots` and the earlier `universe-derived-time` proofs were run break-and-restore against real files. They completed and the tree is verified clean, but the PATTERN is what needs replacing, and doing it at 4 files by hand at the end of a long flight is how a sweep introduces the defect it is fixing. src: 2026-08-03 rejected-call near-miss. open [LC]
- ★TRAINED-LORA-ROADMAP — ⛔ **NEW 2026-08-04. A 9/30-OR-SHORTLY-AFTER BUILD TARGET, NON-NEGOTIABLE (RUSS). NOT A MARKETING CLAIM — THIS IS WHAT HAS TO BE TRUE BEFORE THE WORD "TRAINED" SURVIVES A TECHNICAL AUDIENCE.** ⛔ **VERIFIED FROM VENDOR SOURCE 2026-08-04, DO NOT RE-LITIGATE:** Anthropic does **not** offer Claude fine-tuning through its public API as of 2026; the only path is **Claude 3 Haiku SFT on Amazon Bedrock (us-west-2)** — **Haiku, not Opus, so fine-tuning would make Lora WORSE**, trading the frontier reasoning the product is built on for a smaller model. And fine-tuning adapts **BEHAVIOUR AND FORMAT, NOT KNOWLEDGE**: knowledge the model cannot have is a **RAG problem**, not a training one. ⇒ **THIS CONFIRMS THE EXISTING DIRECTION RATHER THAN CHANGING IT — warm-start Claude = memory + RAG + onboarding, NOT fine-tuning** (P9 MEMORY & LEARNING already carries "warm-start agency brain"). **THE THREE THINGS THAT MAKE "TRAINED" TRUE:** **(a) PER-CLIENT LEARNED LAYER** — persisted and ACCUMULATING: seasonality, normal ranges per metric, conversion lag, which campaigns are structurally different and must not be compared. Built from that client's own complete history, updated as the history grows, injected per query. **This is the part that genuinely improves with time**, and it is the honest referent of "she learns your business." Extends warm-start Claude / P9 Phase 3–4. **(b) CERTIFIED METRIC DEFINITIONS** — [[★SEMANTIC-LAYER]], already ranked INSIDE the 9/30 arc; not restated here (LORAMER_DOCS_SINGLE_OWNER_V1). **(c) CLOSED FEEDBACK LOOP** — corrections and observed outcomes fed back as REUSABLE EXAMPLES, so a correction given once changes later answers. ⛔ **(c) IS THE MISSING PIECE AND IT WAS NOT BANKED ANYWHERE BEFORE TODAY** — P9 names a "nightly learning loop" and dismissed-insight capture, but nothing anywhere turns a human correction into a reusable example. **It is what makes "she learns" literally rather than loosely true, and without it (a) and (b) are just good context assembly.** ⛔ **THE DEFENSIBLE SENTENCE, and it is the deliverable of this item as much as the code is:** *a frontier-general model, whose specialization is a per-client learned layer over complete history, a certified metric layer, and a feedback loop.* ⛔ **NEVER "we fine-tuned Claude."** That sentence is false, checkable in about ten seconds by anyone technical, and would cost more credibility than the feature earns. src: 2026-08-04 Russ. open [NP]
- ★CODE-HYGIENE-SWEEP-KNOWN-HAZARDS — ⛔ **NEW 2026-08-04. CORRECTNESS, NOT TIDINESS. EVERY ITEM HERE IS A SILENT-WRONG-ANSWER GENERATOR *AND* A HAZARD THIS REPO HAD ALREADY DIAGNOSED ONCE WHOSE FIX NEVER REACHED THE NEXT SITE.** That second half is the actual defect: **a solved fix that does not propagate is indistinguishable from no fix**, and every hazard below was solved somewhere and then re-hit somewhere else. **THE HAZARDS:** **(1) LITERAL NUL BYTES IN SOURCE** — hit TWICE on 2026-08-04, the second time inside the yield-ranking script written the same day, while `src/lib/cron-connection-outcome.ts` documents the hazard IN ITS OWN HEADER (*"a raw NUL in a .ts file makes it binary to grep and to every guard that reads source as text"*). ⛔ **AND THE SHARPER STATEMENT, WHICH BELONGS AS A LAW AND NOT A FOOTNOTE: A JOIN THAT MATCHES NOTHING LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE A TRUE ZERO — and `zero is a fact, not a skip` makes that misreading MORE likely, not less, because the codebase is trained to report zeros as findings rather than suspect them. THE RULE: A MATCH RATE OF 0% OR 100% IS A BUG UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE.** On 2026-08-04 a NUL-vs-space separator produced "358 entries returned zero rows", which was dutifully formatted and printed as data. **(2) INCONSISTENT KEY SEPARATORS** — `\x00` in one place and a space in another for the same logical key. One separator, guard-enforced. **(3) TEXT-SEARCH GUARDS** — grep proves a STRING EXISTS, never that CODE BEHAVES; leg (d) of the 2026-08-03 entity-axis guard went GREEN while the behaviour was broken because a constant's NAME survived in a function body. Guards must drive the compiled module wherever the property is behavioural. **(4) `now()` IN PL/pgSQL IS TRANSACTION START** — a 158-second job logged `finished_at == started_at` on 2026-08-04; use `clock_timestamp()`. **(5) INVERTED / MEANING-SHIFTED STAMPS** — [[★DRAIN-CRON-RUNS-ORPHANED]], where a column is NULL on success and populated on failure. Outcome must be an EXPLICIT value, never inferred from a timestamp. **(6) SWALLOWED ERRORS** — `String(e)` on a GoogleAdsFailure emitting the literal `"[object Object]"` (which hid a 9.8% capability gap for an entire flight), and `execFileSync` reporting `"Command failed"` while discarding tsc's actual output. ⛔ **THE DELIVERABLE IS A GUARD PER HAZARD, NOT A CLEANUP PASS.** A cleanup fixes today's instances; a guard is what stops instance N+1, and instance N+1 is the entire point of this item. **RANKED AFTER 9/30 — EXCEPT THE NUL-BYTE GUARD, which is trivial (scan tracked source for `\x00`) and MAY RIDE WITH ANY FLIGHT THAT TOUCHES THE WALK.** src: 2026-08-04 hygiene review. open [LC]
- ★UNIVERSE-50-WINDOW-PROJECTION-ASSUMES-THE-DENSEST-MONTH — ✅ **RESOLVED 2026-08-04 BY A SECOND MEASUREMENT, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE DISK WE ALREADY HAVE IS ENOUGH.** A median-activity window (2025-03-02..03-31, 5,616 account clicks against a median of 4,855 across 49 active months) was walked with the narrowed 346-entry set: **1,568,372 rows · 344 requests · 29m14s · +1.666 GB · 100% INSERT (2,752 rows pre-existed, 1,571,124 after).** **TWO MEASURED POINTS NOW EXIST** — 5,616 clicks → 1,568,372 rows and 66,380 clicks → 4,203,809 rows — which fit **rows ∝ clicks^0.399**, i.e. STRONGLY SUBLINEAR: an 11.8× activity increase produced only a 2.7× row increase, because rows are driven by account STRUCTURE (entities × values × days), not by volume. Applying that fit across the real 52-month shape (49 active, 3 empty) gives **≈83.1M rows ⇒ 64.4 GB/client at the measured 832 B/row, or 88.3 GB at the 1,141 B/row observed here** (that figure is an UPPER bound — the disk delta is a whole-cluster read taken while forward and drain were also writing). ⇒ **PROVISIONED REQUIRED: 218–248 GB. WE HAVE 280 GB. IT FITS, WITH MARGIN, AND NO FURTHER DISK IS NEEDED.** ⛔ **THE OLD 129.3 GB WAS 50 × THE SINGLE BEST MONTH IN FOUR YEARS; the corrected figure is a weighted sum over the months that actually exist.** ⚠ **THE FIT IS TWO POINTS AND CLICKS ARE A PROXY** — it is a far better estimate than either extreme, not a guarantee, and the walk's own window log will replace it with fact as it goes. ORIGINAL ENTRY FOLLOWS. ⛔ **NEW 2026-08-04, AND IT INVALIDATES THE DISK DECISION IN THE CHEAP DIRECTION.** Every projection this arc has produced — 251.6 GB, then 226.7 GB, then the narrowed 129.3 GB — was built by measuring ONE window and multiplying by 50. **THAT ONE WINDOW WAS 2026-03-07..04-05, AND 2026-03 IS THE HIGHEST-CLICK MONTH IN FOAM OH'S ENTIRE ~4-YEAR GOOGLE HISTORY (66,380 clicks).** The account's monthly clicks range from **298 (2022-08) to 66,380 (2026-03) — a 220× spread** across 50 months. - ★BACKFILL-RESERVE-IS-SOFT-ORDERING — ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-04 BY LORAMER_BACKFILL_YIELDS_TO_PRODUCT_V1. THE RESERVE IS NOW A FLOOR, NOT AN ORDERING.** `decidePublishFleetAware()` reads FLEET spend (forward + catchup + drain + unattributed, from `google-op-budget`'s existing reader — that module was NOT modified) plus the backfill's own exact spend, and **holds the full 9,000 product reserve REGARDLESS of what the product has spent**: `publishable = CAP − 9,000 − productSpent − backfillSpent`. ⛔ **THE WALK YIELDS; THE PRODUCT NEVER DOES** — stale data presented as current is worse than history arriving late, and that is the governing law rather than a preference. **NO DEADLOCK IS STRUCTURALLY POSSIBLE: THE YIELD IS ONE-WAY.** Only the backfill consults the fleet and only the backfill stands down; forward/catchup/drain never look at it, so there is no cycle to wait on. **FAIL CLOSED** — a null fleet reading HOLDS, matching google-op-budget's own posture. **A STAND-DOWN IS RECORDED** as `quota_stop` in `universe_window_log` with the governor's arithmetic on the row — extending the existing outcome vocabulary (the exact analogue of `floor_stop`), not a parallel one — and ⛔ **it does NOT settle the entry**, so a walk that yielded all day still reads as OWED and never as finished. ⛔ **THE GUARD CAUGHT THREE BUGS IN MY OWN ARITHMETIC BEFORE ANY OF IT SHIPPED:** the first formulation computed `reserveLeft = RESERVE − productSpent` and published out of the difference, which was backwards in BOTH directions — on a QUIET day it lent out the untouched reserve, and on a HEAVY day (product already past its reserve) it clamped to zero and offered the walk the ENTIRE remaining headroom, so **the most over-subscribed day produced the most generous answer**. Holding the reserve in full makes the ceiling shrink monotonically as the product gets busier, which is the only shape consistent with the law. ⚠ **THE HONEST LIMIT OF THE INSTRUMENT, stated because a governor is only as good as its counter: fleet spend is an ESTIMATE (`connections × 67` from `cron_runs`), not a measurement, and it OMITS the INTELLIGENCE LANE ENTIRELY — `/api/intelligence` makes live Google Ads calls on user page loads and writes no `cron_runs` row.** So the fleet figure UNDER-counts, which is the dangerous direction; the 9,000 held reserve is what absorbs it. Only the backfill's own spend is exact (one `universe_window_log` row = one request). **[[★FLEET-SPEND-OMITS-INTELLIGENCE-LANE]] carries the gap.** ORIGINAL ENTRY FOLLOWS. ⛔ **NEW 2026-08-04. THE RESERVE IS AN ORDERING, NOT A FLOOR, AND ON A HEAVY DRAIN DAY IT STARVES THE WRONG LANE — THE OPPOSITE OF ITS INTENT.** `decidePublish()` in `src/lib/backfill/universe-governor.ts` reads **only the backfill's own spend** — the code says so in terms (*"never a fleet number, because billing the backfill for the drain's requests would stop it for the wrong reason"*). **WHAT IS GUARANTEED:** the backfill never spends more than its 6,000-op allowance. **WHAT IS NOT:** that 9,000 ops remain for forward + drain. The reserves are subtracted from the BACKFILL's ceiling; nothing measures or constrains the other two lanes, and nothing tells the backfill they overran. **THE ARITHMETIC ON A HEAVY DRAIN DAY:** forward 4,000 + drain 8,000 (over its 5,000 reserve) + backfill 6,000 = **18,000 against a 15,000 cap**. The backfill does not back off, because it cannot see the overrun — so the lane that hits the wall is the **DRAIN**, which is live product data, while the 2022 backfill runs on undisturbed. ⛔ **THIS GATES UNATTENDED MULTI-DAY RUNNING.** A 3-day walk is exactly the scenario where a heavy drain day is likely and nobody is watching. It did NOT block the 2026-08-04 flight only because the walk was refused on disk first. ⛔ **NOT FIXED HERE — RUSS EXPLICITLY RULED IT A SEPARATE DECISION**, and it is a real one: the honest fix reads fleet spend before publishing, which means the backfill can be starved by the other lanes instead, and choosing which lane loses is a product call rather than an engineering one. Ranked, not built. src: 2026-08-04 pre-flight §2. open [LC]

- ★UPSTREAM-PATTERN-REVIEW — **NEW 2026-07-30. THIS PROBLEM CLASS IS SOLVED PUBLICLY AND WE HAVE BEEN RE-DERIVING IT, expensively, one defect at a time.** Documented prior art that maps onto laws we invented the hard way: **Airbyte's Google Ads connector clamps requested ranges to the 37-month retention window** — that is our `floor36()`, arrived at after a night of retention-wall surprises. **Fivetran runs a daily ROLLBACK SYNC that re-captures changes falling outside the incremental window** — that is our LORAMER_RESTATEMENT_WINDOW_LAW_V1 (Meta 9d, GA4 7d), which we derived from late-attributed conversions rather than from anyone's docs — **and it uses the Google Ads Change Status Service to fetch only CHANGED entities**, which we do not do at all and which would cut breadth-lap cost against the 15k/day cap. **Standard backfill practice includes PRE/POST CHECKS — row counts, checksums, metric comparisons** — which is exactly what LORAMER_COMPLETION_CLAIM_GATE_V1 turned out to be, built 2026-07-30 after FOUR accidental discoveries of the same missing invariant. ⛔ **AND THE ONE THAT CHALLENGES OUR ARCHITECTURE — clause completed by Russ 2026-07-30.** Datadog considered a **WATERMARK-based** approach to measuring data completeness and **REJECTED IT**: watermarks depend on data arriving within a PREDICTABLE WINDOW, and when data can arrive arbitrarily delayed there is **no reliable point at which to advance one**. Their alternative was to split pipelines into SEGMENTS, track each payload through them, and combine segment-level measurements into overall completeness. **WHY IT CHALLENGES US, RECORDED AS THE FINDING AND NOT AS TRIVIA: our `sync_state` cursors ARE WATERMARKS.** And **LORAMER_RESTATEMENT_WINDOW_LAW_V1 — our OWN banked law — says every platform REVISES DATA AFTER THE FACT** (Meta 9 days minimum, GA4 7, and GA4 dimensional values literally CHANGE during Google's 24-48h processing, which is why the forward-dim lookback exists). **So our own law states that the precondition watermarks require is FALSE for our sources.** That tension is the ROOT of the whole class fixed on 2026-07-29/30: **a cursor asserts a point in time as SETTLED while the data behind it keeps changing.** Every completion-flag defect that night is a symptom of it — the 2026-07-15 sealed Meta breadth cursors reading 13/13 over a permanent hole · ga_dimensional's `done` measuring walk distance · ga_dimensional line 220 sealing on zero work · rangeLap's two identical defects across 22 drain families · run-backfill.ts:268 · and the 51 baselined completion-claim violations. **Not six bugs. ONE architectural assumption, six places.** **LORAMER_COMPLETION_CLAIM_GATE_V1 IS A PARTIAL ANSWER AND SHOULD BE READ AS ONE**: it compares the CLAIM TO THE ROWS instead of trusting the watermark, which is why one comparison caught all four instances at once — but it still lets a watermark BE the claim, and by its own stated limit it cannot tell "the vendor served nothing" from "we never asked". ⛔ **THE SEGMENT-TRACKING ALTERNATIVE IS A DESIGN TO READ, NOT A PLAN TO ADOPT. NO REWRITE IS PROPOSED AND NONE SHOULD BE INFERRED** — recording a tension is not scheduling a migration, and conflating the two is a mistake this repo has already paid for. Source: Datadog engineering, "How we measure data completeness at scale". SHAPE OF THE WORK: read the upstream connectors' documented behaviour BEFORE the next capture-family build, and for each of our banked laws record whether it matches prior art, contradicts it, or is genuinely ours. The cost of not doing this is measurable — every law above was paid for in defects. Cross-ref PROBE-BEFORE-BUILDING and the read-first existence check (twice caught a writer that already existed). src: 2026-07-30 session wrap. open [LC]

IT WAS STATED OUT LOUD. IT DID NOT CONSTRAIN THE ANSWER.** That is the whole finding, and it is why the two classes must not be merged: ★HONESTY-ENFORCERS-MISS-GRAIN-ABSENCE is a PLUMBING defect — the coverage verdict never reaches `query_metrics`/`query_money`, so she cannot know — and its fix is to wire the signal. FIX DIRECTION, not scoped: this is a CONSTRAINT-FOLLOWING problem, so its candidates are prompt-level (a rule that a stated limitation forbids the dependent claim) or a post-hoc check that reads the answer for a named boundary and then for a claim that crosses it — NOT another data signal. src: 2026-08-01 eval run 2. open [LC]

(Corroborating signal: `search_term` and `keyword` day-counts are IDENTICAL in every month — 17/17, 5/5 — because both are Search-only views on one code path.) **THE PRECEDENT ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS REPO AND SHOULD BE COPIED, NOT REINVENTED: the breakdown registry's keyword/PMax SUBSET rule** — a grain that is a SUBSET of the anchor rather than a PARTITION of it is marked WRITE-ONLY and deliberately NOT reconciled, because reconciling a non-partition grain produces FALSE flags that drown the real ones (Gate A: keyword reconcile flagged 21/21 days on a mixed account). **That is this same problem, already solved once, one layer down.** The registry's `additive` / `highCardinality` / `rankBy` flags are the shape: a per-family declaration of expected behaviour, consumed by the verdict. ⛔ **AND A SEPARATE RULE THAT FALLS OUT OF BOTH WITHDRAWALS: ANY COMPLETENESS THRESHOLD MUST BE PER-PLATFORM OR EXPRESSED AS A SHARE OF ACTIVE DAYS — NEVER AN ABSOLUTE DAY COUNT.** A 28-day bar is meaningless on a store platform where a zero-revenue day is normal, and it manufactured two false findings in one evening. Candidate families needing the flag: search_term, keyword (Search-only); discount_code, coupon_code, abandoned_checkout (event-sparse). src: 2026-08-01, replaces two withdrawn findings. open [LC]

- ★COVERAGE-INSTRUMENT-8S-CEILING-DIVERGES — **NEW 2026-08-01. THE SAME WINDOW READS COMPLETE OR UNKNOWN DEPENDING ON WHICH PATH ASKS.** The eval windows were derived through a direct pg session with `statement_timeout = 600s`; the LIVE instrument goes through PostgREST and is bound by the **8-second** ceiling, returning UNKNOWN above it (`getBreakdownCoverage` fails to UNKNOWN rather than to an optimistic COMPLETE — correct, and the reason the divergence is safe rather than dangerous). **Foam OH meta is the known offender and is named in coverage.ts's own header as still exceeding the ceiling.** So a window this anchoring calls COMPLETE can read UNKNOWN to Lora, and the eval would be grading against a coverage fact the live product cannot itself observe. ⛔ **THE DATA IS THE SAME; THE INSTRUMENT DIFFERS** — which makes this a statement about measurement, not about capture, and it must not be recorded as a coverage gap. Cross-ref [[★BREAKDOWN-COVERAGE-UNKNOWN-CONFLATES-TIMEOUT]] (shipped: UNKNOWN now carries its reason, so a timeout is distinguishable from an idle account — that fix is exactly what makes this divergence diagnosable rather than invisible).
