- ★TWO-EVAL-HARNESSES-ONE-JUDGE — **NEW 2026-08-01. TWO EVAL HARNESSES EXIST, THEY GRADE DIFFERENTLY, AND ONLY ONE CAN JUDGE. NOT RESOLVED TONIGHT — RECORDED SO THE SPLIT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN ACCIDENT.** (1) `tests/lora-evals/run-evals.mjs` + `golden-set.json` (28 questions, the shipped accuracy gate): scorer is **DETERMINISTIC REGEX + number matching**, no LLM judge. Its `honesty` type is one fixed phrase list plus a $0-fabrication check. ⛔ **ITS CASES CARRY A `rubric` FIELD AND THE SCORER NEVER READS IT** — the rubric is documentation that reads like an assertion, which is its own small instance of prose-is-not-a-guard. (2) `tests/lora-evals/run-l2-evals.mjs` + `l2-seed-set.json` (10 questions, newer): **HAS an LLM judge** (`JUDGE_MODEL`, validated 117×3 zero flips on the rejudge contract) and **COMPUTES ground truth from `metrics_daily` at run time** from a `truth` spec rather than from hand-typed numbers. **WHY IT MATTERS AND IS NOT COSMETIC:** the regex scorer **cannot grade the UNVERIFIED-BOUNDARY type at all** — the passing answer ('we do not hold it, and whether Google would serve it is unconfirmed') and the failing answer ('we do not hold it, Google only keeps 90 days') both match the same honesty regex, and the second asserts a vendor fact we have never established. Building 100 questions onto the regex harness would have silently scored that distinction as a pass. **WHAT WAS DONE 2026-08-01, deliberately the smaller move:** the judge was extracted to a shared `boundary-judge.mjs` and the V2 set was built into the **golden-set lineage** (`run-evals.mjs --set eval-set-v2.json`), because V2 is a golden-set successor by its own declaration and a THIRD runner would widen the split. **WHAT IS STILL OPEN:** the two harnesses still have different case schemas (`assert` block vs `truth` spec), different scoring philosophies (hand-typed expected values vs DB-computed truth), and different notions of what a pass is. ⚠ **AND THE TENSION IS REAL, NOT JUST DUPLICATION:** L2's DB-computed truth is the better engineering — a number a human typed goes stale — but V2 section 3 rules it out for this set on the ground that **truth read from our own store makes the eval circular**, since a question about an uncaptured window would score correct against an empty ground truth. Both positions are right about different question types. Resolving the split means deciding WHICH questions may take DB truth and which require an external read, and that is a design decision, not a refactor. src: 2026-08-01 100-question eval build. open [LC]
- ★FLIGHT-REPORT-NAMES-ASSERTED-MECHANISMS — ⛔ **7th PRECEDENT ADDED 2026-08-04 AND IT IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE ONE YET: [[LORAMER_CONDITIONAL_RULE_LOST_ITS_CONDITION_V1]] — "adding preview domains revokes GA refresh tokens", a mechanism Google's documentation does not support, asserted and re-asserted until it blocked the entire chat-UI arc for OVER A WEEK.** The others were wrong beliefs that cost a debugging round; this one cost an arc. ⛔ **AND IT ADDS A FAILURE MODE THE FIRST SIX DID NOT HAVE: the assertion did not start as an invention — it started as a TRUE, CONDITIONAL rule (Lesson 42, valid while a Google verification was open) and became false by having its condition stripped in restatement.** The condition ended 2026-07-17; the rule was written down 2026-07-27 still calling adwords "under review"; each retelling dropped more qualification until the surviving sentence named a mechanism that was never in the source at all — Lesson 42's own list is *app name, domains, scopes, homepage/privacy/TOS, logo*, every one a CONSENT SCREEN field, and a redirect URI is OAuth CLIENT config. ⇒ **LAW 9 IS NOT ONLY ABOUT INVENTED MECHANISMS. A TRUE RULE DECAYS INTO AN ASSERTED ONE WHEN ITS CONDITION IS NOT CARRIED WITH IT.** THE ENFORCEMENT: bank the CONDITION and HOW TO TEST IT in the same sentence as the rule; and when a rule blocks work, RE-READ THE SOURCE rather than the latest restatement. **A rule whose condition is not written down cannot be retired, only obeyed.** ORIGINAL ENTRY FOLLOWS. **NEW 2026-08-01. THE ENFORCER FOR [[LORAMER_ESSENCE_LAW_9_V1]], AND IT IS THE EXECUTOR'S HALF ON PURPOSE.** REQUIREMENT: every flight report carries a required line naming **any mechanism the instruction ASSERTED, and whether it was VERIFIED, FALSIFIED, or NOT CHECKED**. ⛔ **EMPTY IS A VALID VALUE AND MUST BE STATED EXPLICITLY** — 'instruction asserted no mechanism' is a complete answer; OMITTING the line is not, because silence is indistinguishable from having skipped the check. Same posture as the WEB-FIRST header's 'searched X, none found'. **WHY NOT A SCRIPT:** law 9 binds the INSTRUCTION, and prose in a doc is not a guard (banked law) — but a checker that judges whether an instruction ASSERTS A MECHANISM is a judgment about natural language, which is precisely the COMPREHENSION-NOT-MATCHING boundary LORAMER_DOC_OWNERSHIP_GUARD_V1 refused on the record. **THE EXECUTOR'S HALF IS DECIDABLE** — the executor knows what it was told and what it found — so the rule converts a conversation-layer defect into a line in a report instead of something Russ has to catch by reading carefully. **PRECEDENT FOR THE SHAPE, and it should be copied rather than reinvented: LORAMER_WEB_FIRST_DIAGNOSIS_V1 (HANDOFF:259)** — a law living in ESSENCE, made VISIBLE by a required report header, enforced AT DELIVERY (a headerless paste is malformed and rejected on sight, without reading the content). ⚠ **THE PRECEDENT ALSO BANKED THIS ENFORCER'S LIMIT, VERBATIM, AND IT APPLIES UNCHANGED:** 'no guard can see whether a search actually happened BEFORE the code existed — the temporal order of search-vs-authorship is invisible to any check.' The requirement here is that the line be produced **BEFORE building, not as a postmortem** — and by that same argument the BEFORE is NOT mechanically inspectable. Only the line's PRESENCE is. Do not mistake the line for full enforcement. **PRECEDENT, 2026-07-31/08-01 — three false premises, and THE TWO FAILURE SHAPES ARE DIFFERENT, which is why 'before, not after' is the load-bearing clause:** (1) **withGoogleRetry** — the premise WAS verified and WAS reported, but only AFTER the design had been built around it; a postmortem line would have scored this a clean pass while the flight had already been shaped by a false claim. (2) **catchup fillDays ordering** — the stated hypothesis was TESTED rather than the ordering being READ FIRST; the instruction supplied the question and the executor answered that question instead of establishing the ground truth. (3) **the search-term floor** — asserted as a vendor wall, actually `DEFAULT_DAYS = 90` in our own backfill.  **(5) ADDED 2026-08-03 — ★MCP-BASELINE-HEAD-TO-HEAD AND ★USAGE-CAP-ABSENT: a false claim about OUR OWN RECORDS.** Both were cited across 2026-08-03 as though banked; neither existed. A `[[★TOKEN]]` costs nothing to type and reads exactly like a citation of something real. **(6) ADDED 2026-08-04 — THE SUPABASE BILLING ALERT THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** Russ was told twice to set a spend-threshold notification; Supabase's own cost-control doc says the Spend Cap offers no per-item budgets and no cost-threshold notifications. **Same shape as (4) — a UI affordance asserted without a source — and it cost a human two trips to look for something that was never there.** ⛔ **THE RULE THAT FALLS OUT OF (4) AND (6): when naming a vendor UI affordance nobody here has SEEN, say so.** **(4) ADDED 2026-08-03 — the GOOGLE ADS API CENTER OPERATION COUNTER, and it is the FOURTH shape: a mechanism asserted for a screen that DOES NOT EXIST.** [[★GAQL-OP-METER]] was banked, sharpened, ranked as "the highest-value open item in the repo" and handed to Russ as a five-minute human read of a per-day operation count in the API Center. That screen shows the developer token, the access level and the API contact email — no usage counter, no remaining-ops figure; Google's own support says remaining daily operations cannot be read and must be tracked client-side. **The task was un-doable for the whole time it sat on the list**, and what actually closed it was READING THE VENDOR'S RATE SHEET (1 query = 1 operation; valid-`next_page_token` continuations free) — a document that existed the entire time. ⛔ **THE SHAPE THAT IS NEW: (1)–(3) were false claims about OUR code or the vendor's DATA. (4) is a false claim about a vendor UI, and it is worse, because a task assigned to a HUMAN produces no error, no failing guard and no log line when the human simply never finds the screen — it just sits.** WEB-FIRST would have closed this on day one. HOME: the flight-report contract in **LORAMER_HANDOFF.md** (REPORT FORMAT at :40, the WEB-FIRST three-field header at :259) — ⛔ **NOT a .mjs guard**; it is a report-FORMAT rule and belongs where the other report-format rules live. src: 2026-08-01 law 9 bank. open [LC]
- ★EXTERNAL-DOCS-OUTSIDE-THE-REPO — **NEW 2026-08-01. - ★VERCEL-SILENT-NO-DEPLOY — **NEW 2026-08-01. A PUSH LANDED ON main AND VERCEL BUILT NOTHING, SILENTLY. THE FIX WAS BELIEVED LIVE AND WAS NOT.** `363631d` (LORAMER_QUOTA_ARM_AT_ERROR_BOUNDARY_V1) reached `origin/main` at 00:50Z; **fifteen minutes later Vercel had created ZERO deployment records** (`list_deployments since=00:40Z` → count 0) and `app.loramer.com` was still serving `dpl_HQpgy5ce`, the previous commit's build. Every other push that day deployed in **~90 seconds**. A missed GitHub webhook — nothing was wrong with the commit. WORKAROUND USED, and the shape of it is deliberate: an **empty re-trigger commit** (`8bf18ff`) so the build stays tied to a git sha. ⛔ **DID NOT side-load a build via the Vercel deploy tool** — a deployment untied to a sha makes 'what is live' unanswerable from git, which is worse than the outage it patches. ⛔ **NOTHING IN THE CURRENT SETUP WOULD HAVE SURFACED THIS.** There is no post-push deploy assertion; the ONLY reason it was caught is that a human step in the flight said 'confirm deploy READY' and someone looked. A push report that says 'pushed' is not evidence of a deploy, and every ship report in this repo has been treating the two as the same fact. **WHETHER A MECHANICAL CHECK IS POSSIBLE IS OPEN** — it cannot live in `npm run guard` (that runs BEFORE the push, and on Vercel itself); it would have to be a post-push poll comparing the live deployment's `githubCommitSha` against `git rev-parse HEAD`, which is a new class of check for this repo (asserts against a THIRD-PARTY control plane, and fails for reasons outside the codebase). Decide deliberately before building it. src: 2026-08-01 sentinel ship. open [LC]
- ★LORA-OVER-WARNS-READ-FAILURES-AS-CAPTURE-FAILURE — **NEW 2026-08-01. THE OTHER TAIL OF LAW 6, AND IT IS A REAL FAILURE RATHER THAN A SAFE DIRECTION TO ERR IN.** In the Gate-B read-back Lora stated **'Google capture is currently failing (last captured day = 2026-07-30, failing since 2026-08-01 01:31 UTC)'**. BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG IN THE SAME SENTENCE: the 01:31Z signal was **three READ-path failures** — Gate-B dashboard loads against an exhausted token — not capture failures; and **'last captured day 07-30' IS NORMAL at 01:00Z**, because forward capture runs 08–10Z, so 07-31 had simply not been captured yet. She rendered a routine hour-of-day as a defect. ⛔ **THE POINT IS NOT THAT SHE WAS WRONG, IT IS THE DIRECTION.** ESSENCE law 6 pushes hard against UNDER-warning (a confident answer over an uncaptured window) and every enforcer built for it — coverage notes, empty-state headers, degraded lines, the quota caveat — pushes the same way. Nothing pushes back. **A CAVEAT THAT DOES NOT BEAR ON THE ANSWER IS NOISE, AND NOISE IS WHAT TRAINS A USER TO STOP READING CAPTIONS** — at which point the caveats that DO matter stop working too, and law 6 loses by the route it never watches. Same turn also contained the correct behaviour (the quota outage line, which DID bear on the answer), so the fix is not 'fewer caveats' — it is a relevance test: does this caveat change how the number should be read? A last-captured-day inside the normal capture lag does not. ⚠ **DO NOT FIX BY LOOSENING THE HONESTY BLOCKS** — the failure is a MISSING DISTINCTION (read-path failure vs capture failure; normal lag vs a gap), not excess candour. src: 2026-08-01 Gate-B read-back. open [LC]
- ★BUDGET-IS-A-DOOR-CHECK-NOT-A-METER — **NEW 2026-08-01. THE GOOGLE OP BUDGET IS A PER-FIRE ADMISSION CHECK, NOT A SPEND METER. ONE FIRE CAN SPEND THE ENTIRE DAY BEFORE THE NEXT ONE IS TOLD.** `googleBudgetHold` is computed ONCE per invocation at `catchup/route.ts:272` and then applied per-client at `:594` (`fillDays = (googleQuotaPaused || googleBudgetHold) ? [] : …`) using that same value. Nothing re-reads inside the loop, so a fire that passes the gate then spends without limit across 18 connections × N days each. **MEASURED 2026-07-31: catchup burned 13,869 raw requests in FIVE fires between 11:19Z and 11:59Z — ~2,774 per fire against a CATCHUP_ALLOCATION of 4,500 ops ≈ 3,000 raw requests. One fire is the whole allocation.** The lane then read as 92% of all fleet spend (forward 1,206 · catchup 13,869 · drain 0; fleet ~22,613 ops against a 15,000 cap — a 51% overshoot) and the developer-scope token was exhausted for the rest of the day. ⛔ **NOT FIXED BY EITHER 2026-07-31 BUDGET FIX, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** LORAMER_NO_CACHED_DB_READ_V1 made the gate read FRESH and LORAMER_GOOGLE_OP_BUDGET_LANE_ACCOUNTING_V2 made it read the RIGHT LANE — both correct, both about the ACCURACY of a number consulted once. The defect is the CADENCE: an accurate number checked once per fire still admits an unbounded fire. Fix is a decrement-as-you-spend counter, or a re-read inside the per-client loop. ⚠ **DO NOT BUNDLE THIS INTO AN UNRELATED FLIGHT** — it touches the loop that spends real quota, and a wrong ratchet here either burns the cap or starves capture entirely. Deliberately left unfixed when found. src: 2026-07-31 sentinel diagnosis. open [LC]
- ★WITHGOOGLERETRY-TRANSIENT-NEVER-MATCHES — **NEW 2026-08-01. A RETRY WRAPPER WHOSE TRANSIENT TEST MATCHES NOTHING, IN THE ONE FILE WHOSE JOB IS RETRYING.** `backfill/retry.ts` `withGoogleRetry` tests `TRANSIENT.test(String(e?.message || ''))`, but a google-ads-api rejection carries its detail on `errors[]` and leaves `.message` EMPTY — so for GoogleAdsFailure rejections the test matches NOTHING and the exponential backoff never fires. **THIS IS A KNOWN, DOCUMENTED CLASS IN THIS REPO:** `backfill/gaql-with-retry.ts` records the identical defect in its own header ("the prior /…/.test(e.message) matched nothing and neither quota NOR transient detection ever fired") and fixed it there by reading `err.errors[0]` via `classifyGoogleAdsError`. The same fix was never applied to `withGoogleRetry`, which serves the account adapter and the dimensional backfill. **PARTIALLY ADDRESSED 2026-08-01:** LORAMER_QUOTA_ARM_AT_ERROR_BOUNDARY_V1 added `classifyGoogleAdsError` to this wrapper for the QUOTA path, so quota is now detected and armed correctly; the TRANSIENT path was deliberately left alone because changing it alters retry behaviour on live backfill writers and belongs in its own flight with its own proof. **SO TODAY: transient google failures on those two lanes get ZERO of their four configured retries and surface as hard failures on the first attempt.** src: 2026-07-31 sentinel fix, found while wiring the boundary. open [LC]

- ★ META-BACKFILL-OBSERVED-ZERO — FLEET-WIDE, not one client. FORWARD and BACKFILL disagree about what a dormant day looks like. Forward (meta-metrics-row.ts) pushes the account row UNCONDITIONALLY from totals, so a dormant account still gets a daily $0 anchor row. Backfill (fetchMetaDailyMetrics → runBackfill) writes ONLY the days Meta returns, so a dormant stretch walked by backfill produces NO rows. Same day, two different truths depending on which path saw it. CONSEQUENCES, both observed 2026-07-19: (1) it is why Influential Drones' dormant stretch holds zero rows once forward broke — backfill could never have covered for it; (2) it makes the standard-C landing gate's PARTITIONING anchor untrustworthy, because "an account row exists" stops meaning "we looked at this day" (the false Ennis flag this morning came from an anchor that included days no breakdown could ever exist for). FIX, SCOPED NOT AUTHORED: make Meta backfill emit a $0 account row for days Meta returns empty, matching forward's observed-zero. This is NOT a fabricated zero and does NOT violate the false-zero law — it records the SAME observed-empty that forward already records; the distinction is observed-empty (Meta answered, nothing ran) vs invented (we never asked). BLAST RADIUS: the SHARED backfill path (run-backfill.ts + the meta adapter), so every platform riding that engine must be read first — a read-first scope pass before any authoring, no exceptions. src: 2026-07-19 Meta unseal recon. open [LC]

SOURCES, per vendor: **Meta = the response header itself**, and it is the strongest of the five because it reports what we GOT rather than what is current · **Google = the npm registry JSON for `google-ads-api`** (its major tracks the API major), with sunset derivable as release-month + 12 rather than scraped · **Shopify = `{ publicApiVersions { handle supported displayName } }` on the GraphQL Admin API — the missing release notes do NOT foreclose automating Shopify, because the API answers about itself** · **GA4 = omit entirely**, v1beta is the only version and a permanently-green row is noise · **Woo = do not poll**, it is a read against the merchant's own box and wc/v3 has been the only production namespace for years. TRIGGERS: **WARN** when a pin is behind current. **FAIL at sunset MINUS 30 DAYS, not on the date** — a hard fail on the sunset date is a failure you discover from production breakage, not from the guard. **AND THE META TRIGGER IS DIFFERENT ON PURPOSE: FAIL on `sent ≠ served`, read from the header** — strictly stronger than any sunset check, because Meta auto-upgrades instead of failing, and this trigger would have fired on day one where a date-based check missed it for months. - ★QUERY-BREAKDOWN-NO-STALENESS — **T3, HIGH — FLEET-WIDE LIVE CORRECTNESS BUG.** The stale signal exists ONLY on query_metrics: runQueryMetricsTool attaches the completeness CONTRIBUTION from coverage (per platform), but runQueryBreakdownTool attaches ONLY a topN/subset note — NO coverage, NO contribution, NO staleness annotation. So for ANY breakdown question on ANY platform (channels, sources, geo, demographics, search terms, placements, …), Lora reports whatever rows exist AS CURRENT, however old they are. Presenting STALE data as current is WORSE than a false zero — nothing looks wrong. FIX: query_breakdown must carry a per-FAMILY staleness signal the way query_metrics carries a per-platform one. - ★COVERAGE-IS-BASE-GRAIN-ONLY — ⚙ **RESOLVER SHIPPED 2026-07-30 (LORAMER_COVERAGE_BREAKDOWN_GRAIN_V1 — DECISIONS owns the law, the two stacked defects, the three-state vocabulary and the honest limits). NOT YET WIRED, so the live behaviour below is UNCHANGED.** What shipped: `resolveBreakdownCoverage` (pure, set-difference of base-ACTIVE days minus breakdown days, per the banked per-platform activity predicate) + `getBreakdownCoverage` (RPC-backed, UNKNOWN on any failure) + migration 046 (read-only function) + the 31st guard. **WHAT IS STILL OPEN AND IS THE WHOLE REMAINING ITEM: no caller reads it.** The seven live readers — `claude-tools.ts`, `intelligence/route.ts`, and the five `-next` routes (client-metrics, money, card-roas, ga-overview, store-stats) — were deliberately left untouched, because wiring it is the moment Lora's caveats and the dashboard labels change and that needs its own blast-radius conversation. Also still open: per-family freshness has a first/last date now but no STALENESS threshold, and `sync_state` is still keyed (client_id, platform) with no per-family cursor, so "this family stopped" still has nowhere to live. [[★QUERY-BREAKDOWN-NO-STALENESS]] remains blocked on the WIRING, not on the resolver. ORIGINAL ENTRY KEPT VERBATIM: the STRUCTURAL CAUSE of ★QUERY-BREAKDOWN-NO-STALENESS. coverage.ts minMaxFor reads ONLY entity_level='account' AND breakdown_type='' AND breakdown_value='' (the account BASE grain); stale_tail fires when THAT base lastCaptured falls ≥ LAG_TOLERANCE_DAYS behind the capturable frontier. It NEVER inspects breakdown rows. So a FAMILY going quiet while the account base keeps flowing is invisible to QUERY_COMPLETENESS — per-family freshness does not exist ANYWHERE. Related: sync_state is keyed by (client_id, platform) with NO per-family cursor, so there is nowhere a "family stopped" state could even be represented. src: 2026-07-24 GA freeze diagnosis. open [LC]

TWO ASKS, DIFFERENT SHAPES: · FILTER (the real build) — "what's wasting money" = spend>0 AND conversions=0, ranked; RANK-INDEPENDENT (the biggest waste is often #1 — Escential's "essential oils" $155 / 34 clicks / 0 conv sits at the top), no paging needed. · OFFSET (cheap, rides along) — LIMIT/OFFSET on the bounded path, array slice on the unbounded path. ⚠ VOLUME FLOOR REQUIRED: zero-conversions catches dead terms AND terms with 2 clicks that never had a chance — naming those is confidently-wrong advice, same class as the Display hour-0 midnight bid-down. Floor threshold is Russ's call, unset. - ★ G2.5 — GEO ABSENCE DIAGNOSIS ("where am I blind?") — **POST-LAUNCH, ordered AFTER ★G2.** WHY: Lora can say what happened somewhere; she CANNOT say where NOTHING happened. Absence is never served by any platform — Google returns zero rows for zero-activity geos (banked 2026-06-28; NOT a false-zero bug, correct behavior). Absence must therefore be COMPUTED at question-time: targeted universe MINUS observed rows.
- ★ G2.6 — DENOMINATOR LAYER (cross-cutting normalization; NOT a geo feature) — **POST-LAUNCH, ordered AFTER ★G2; does NOT gate G2 or G2.5.** WHY — THE MOAT CASE: GA says Wyoming sends high organic traffic; Google says zero impressions there. "Demand exists and you are not buying it" is multi-source-provenance law at its sharpest — the value is explaining WHY sources disagree, and presence-vs-absence is the sharpest disagreement. Same shape for Shopify conversion rate by state, GA sessions, Google impressions. Any geo dimension can borrow it.

THREE DESIGN CONSTRAINTS, each a way this ships BROKEN: (1) ATTRIBUTION IS NOT SHARE — the anomaly is a delta against ITS OWN baseline, not its share of the total; naive top-N names the biggest line item every night and trains users to ignore the bar. THIS item is the opposite failure and the harder one: §A reads GREEN while a BODY section is stale — B/C/D/F/G/H/I are only as fresh as the last regeneration, and hash equality proves the file was not edited behind our back, never which block the body came from. src: prior queue + 2026-07-27. open [LC]
- ★DIGEST-§L-CROSSREF-INHERITS-OPEN — **NEW 2026-08-03, FOUND BY CLOSING [[★GAQL-OP-METER]], AND IT FALSIFIES AN INVARIANT THE GENERATOR ASSERTS ABOUT ITSELF IN A COMMENT.** `scripts/build-resume-digest.mjs` states, at the head of §L: *"STATUS COMES FROM THE SAME WALK AND THE SAME statusIsDone AS §H, so the index and the open-queue list cannot disagree."* ⛔ **THEY CAN, AND TODAY THEY DO.** §H is keyed on the ITEM: ★GAQL-OP-METER's own entry is closed, so its header is correctly ABSENT from the open-queue list. §L is keyed on the ★TOKEN and `bump()` ORs `open` across **every queue item whose text CONTAINS the token** — so the two cross-references written into still-open entries today ([[★GAQL-OP-COUNT-DISCREPANCY]]'s pointer and [[★FLIGHT-REPORT-NAMES-ASSERTED-MECHANISMS]]'s fourth precedent) each mark the token OPEN. **RESULT, live in this digest: §H omits it as closed while §L line reads `★GAQL-OP-METER — OPEN`.** ⛔ **THE PERVERSE INCENTIVE IS THE REAL COST, not the one wrong line: the way to make §L read correctly is to STOP CROSS-REFERENCING A CLOSED ITEM** — i.e. the mechanism punishes exactly the linking discipline the docs are built on, and the cheap "fix" is to silently drop the `★` from a citation, which hides the defect and degrades the doc. It was NOT done here; the cross-references stand and this entry is the record instead. ⚠ **SECOND SYMPTOM, SAME ROOT, PRE-EXISTING:** that §L line also reads `last 2026-09-30` — a FUTURE date, inherited from some other entry's text that merely mentions the token, because `latestDate` is likewise computed over the mentioning block rather than the owning one. ⛔ **SCOPE, STATED SO IT IS NOT OVER-READ: THIS IS A REPORTING DEFECT IN A GENERATED INDEX, NOT A STATUS ERROR IN THE QUEUE.** The QUEUE is right, §H is right, §L is wrong, and §L is the surface a resuming session skims for "is this still open" — which is how a closed item gets relitigated. **FIX SHAPE (not built, docs-only flight):** attribute a token's status ONLY to the item that OWNS it (its header token) and count mere mentions as references, or emit `OPEN(owner) · mentioned-by N` rather than collapsing both into one boolean. ⛔ **AND THE COMMENT MUST CHANGE WITH THE CODE** — a generator asserting an invariant it does not hold is the same class as a green check answering a narrower question than the reader assumes. src: 2026-08-03 ★GAQL-OP-METER closure. open [LC]
- ★WALK-HAS-NO-LIVENESS-DETECTOR — **NEW 2026-08-05. THE WALK CAN STOP PARTWAY AND EVERY SURFACE READS FINE.** DECISIONS LORAMER_QUEUE_MESSAGES_DIE_SILENTLY_V1 owns the vendor behaviour; not restated here. **THE REQUIREMENT: something must be able to say "the walk is supposed to be running and it is not."** Today nothing can. ⛔ **WHY IT IS HARD, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-DERIVED FROM SCRATCH:** **(1)** expiry is SILENT — no log, no event, no dead-letter queue, nothing to subscribe to; the message is deleted server-side and our code never runs. **(2)** from outside, a dead chain and a healthy long backoff are IDENTICAL — both produce no new `universe_window_log` rows, and after 32 attempts the vendor's own forced backoff makes quiet periods normal. **(3)** ABSENCE OF ROWS IS ALSO THE CORRECT SIGNAL FOR THREE LEGITIMATE STATES — a `quota_stop` stand-down, a `floor_stop`, and a walk that has genuinely finished (every entry sealed at the vendor floor) — so "no rows for N minutes" cannot distinguish stopped-correctly from died-silently. **(4)** THE MISSING PRIMITIVE IS A RUN-LEVEL RECORD: we have per-entry state (`universe_run_state`) and per-window rows (`universe_window_log`) and NOTHING that says a RUN is open, what it expected to do, and when it last made progress. Without that, any watchdog is comparing against an intention nobody wrote down. **(5)** the detector CANNOT live in the consumer — a dead chain runs no code — so it must be an external cron or a check on a surface a human already reads. ⛔ **NOT DESIGNED IN THIS FLIGHT, DELIBERATELY.** **ON THE EXPLICIT TTL QUESTION (a code change on publish, and therefore ⛔ ONE THAT CANNOT REACH A CHAIN ALREADY RUNNING ON A PINNED DEPLOYMENT — it protects the NEXT walk, never the current one): IT CUTS BOTH WAYS AND IS NOT CHOSEN HERE.** A SHORTER TTL fails FASTER and LOUDER — the walk dies sooner after a stall, so the gap between "it stopped" and "we could have known" shrinks, and a stuck chain stops burning retry attempts against a wall; the cost is that any outage longer than the TTL — a Supabase blip, a bad deploy, an operator halt exactly like 2026-08-05's — becomes PERMANENT WORK LOSS rather than a pause the queue absorbs. A LONGER TTL (up to the 7-day maximum) SURVIVES those outages and resumes on its own; the cost is that a genuinely poisoned chain retries for a week, and the silent-death window it is meant to protect against simply moves further out. **Neither is safe without (1)–(5) above: with no liveness detector, a long TTL hides the failure and a short TTL creates it.** THAT is the coupling, and it is the reason this item exists rather than a TTL setting. **WHERE IT FALLS AND WHY, stated rather than ranked:** it is the SAME CLASS as the three silent-data-loss findings already banked under [[★PIPELINE-RESILIENCE-LAYER]] — one emoji halting a 33-report lap, a missing key freezing twelve Shopify families for eight days, and weeks of silent `google_geo` statement timeouts — each found BY ACCIDENT rather than by an alarm. It sits BEHIND the walk actually resuming (flight 2 + the re-release), because a liveness detector for a walk that is deliberately stopped is worth nothing this week; and it sits AHEAD of new capture surface (e.g. [[★PMAX-SEARCH-TERMS-NEVER-QUERIED]]) on the argument that an undetected stop invalidates any completeness claim made about what was captured — which is the governing law's own standard, not a preference. src: 2026-08-05 vendor-doc read + the 14:19Z halt. open
- ★CHROME-IOS-COMPOSER-THREE-SYMPTOMS — ⛔ **MEASURED VERDICT 2026-08-05 18:22–18:23Z: THE offsetTop THEORY IS KILLED. 15 SAMPLES, REAL DEVICE, iPhone / iOS 26.2 / Chrome CriOS 151, Foam OH, TWO FULL KEYBOARD CYCLES.** `visualViewport.offsetTop` on BOTH after-dismissal samples (18:23:00.723Z and 18:23:27.383Z) reads **0**, and reads 0 on **14 of 15 samples overall** — the single exception is **−7 at 18:22:40.740Z**, transient rubber-band overscroll at the top of the document (pageTop and scrollY are −7 in the same sample), not a keyboard artefact. **Apple thread 800154 does NOT reproduce here, and the inset formula is EXONERATED.** Symptoms (1) content-below-composer and (2) dead white gap are therefore NOT one defect via a stale `offsetTop`, and **no replacement candidate is established by this data — a keyboard cycle was captured, the SYMPTOM was not.** ⛔ Per the ★UI-OVERFLOW method failure, no fifth theory is offered here. ⚠ **WHAT THE SAMPLES DID ESTABLISH, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE THEORY THEY KILLED — see DECISIONS [[LORAMER_LAYOUT_VIEWPORT_TRACKS_VISUAL_ON_CHROME_IOS_V1]]: `document.documentElement.clientHeight` EQUALLED `visualViewport.height` ON ALL 15 SAMPLES, INCLUDING 763→424 WITH THE KEYBOARD UP.** Consequence for this item: `docH − vvH` is always 0, so **the DERIVED `--lora-kb-inset` is 0 on every sample** (derived from the code's own formula `raw = docH − offsetTop − vvH; inset = raw > 100 ? raw : 0`, never measured) — **the entire keyboard-lift mechanism is INERT on the primary Gate-B browser**, and the composer is held up only by `position: sticky` against a viewport that is itself shrinking. ▶ NEXT: capture a run in which the symptom is VISIBLE on screen, not merely a keyboard cycle. ORIGINAL ENTRY BELOW. **NEW 2026-08-05, AND THE REASON IT IS NEW IS THE FINDING: THESE THREE DEFECTS HAVE EXISTED ONLY IN CHAT HISTORY AND APPEAR NOWHERE IN THIS REPO.** Grep proof at banking time: "white gap" 0 hits, "caret" 0 relevant hits, no entry names any of them. A defect that is not in the queue does not exist to a future session — same failure class as [[★CHAT-PROMPT-ASSEMBLY-DOUBLE-FETCH]], which lived in DECISIONS and in zero queue items. **THE THREE SYMPTOMS, on Chrome iOS (the PRIMARY Gate-B target per LORAMER_GATE_B_TARGET_IS_CHROME_IOS_V1), on the mobile Lora page:** (1) content sits BELOW the composer · (2) a DEAD WHITE GAP appears · (3) the CARET escapes the input. ⛔ **THEY ARE PROBABLY TWO DEFECTS, NOT ONE AND NOT THREE, AND THE DISCRIMINATING TEST IS A SINGLE NUMBER.** Apple developer thread 800154 reports that iOS 26 does not reset `visualViewport.offsetTop` to 0 after keyboard dismissal. **AS WRITTEN THAT LEAD IS KILLED FOR THIS PAGE — nothing in its chain is `position:fixed`** (header `sticky top:0`, composer `sticky bottom:var(--lora-kb-inset)`, and the stylesheet says so in its own header). ⛔ **BUT THE SAME VENDOR BUG REACHES US THROUGH OUR OWN ARITHMETIC:** `LoraPageClient` computes `raw = docH - (vv.offsetTop || 0) - vv.height`, so a stale non-zero `offsetTop` yields a non-zero inset with NO keyboard present, the sticky composer stays lifted, and that accounts for symptoms (1) and (2) with ONE mechanism. **Symptom (3) is a different class** — the textarea's own `max-height:120px` scroll, or iOS scrolling the focused node into a viewport it mis-measures — and is not explained by the inset. ▶ **TO SETTLE: read `visualViewport.offsetTop` AFTER the keyboard is dismissed. NON-ZERO ⇒ (1)+(2) are one defect with one fix. ZERO ⇒ the inset formula is exonerated and it is a different hunt.** ⛔ **NO DEPLOY IS NEEDED TO GET THAT NUMBER** — see [[★CHAT-PROBE-DISPLAY-CANNOT-SHOW-DISMISSAL]]. ⛔ **PERMANENTLY CLOSED, DO NOT PROPOSE:** `dvh` as the keyboard fix (it resolves to the LARGE viewport and never moves on iOS) and `maximumScale:1`. Public advice recommends dvh almost universally; it is wrong for us and was proven wrong on device. ⚠ The desktop shelf's `.scrim` IS `position:fixed; inset:0`, so thread 800154 applies to it LITERALLY — inert on desktop with no keyboard, exposed on a ≥768px tablet. src: 2026-08-05 recon. open ⛔ **FIRST HARD NUMBER ON THE OVERHANG, 2026-08-07 ~05:0xZ, Chrome iOS, from Russ's own screenshot of the frame probe — AND IT IS THE CAPTURE THIS ITEM'S OWN 'NEXT' ASKED FOR ('capture a run in which the SYMPTOM is VISIBLE on screen, not merely a keyboard cycle'). KEYBOARD UP: `docH 424 · panelBottom 1987`. KEYBOARD DOWN, same surface: `docH 763 · panelBottom 763` — EXACTLY EQUAL, which is correct. ⇒ **WITH THE KEYBOARD UP THE PANEL'S BOTTOM EDGE SITS 1,563px BELOW DOCUMENT HEIGHT.** ⚠ **NOT A DISTINCT DEFECT — IT BELONGS HERE**, and the docH values corroborate this item exactly: 763→424 is the same pair already banked in [[LORAMER_LAYOUT_VIEWPORT_TRACKS_VISUAL_ON_CHROME_IOS_V1]] (`documentElement.clientHeight` EQUALS `visualViewport.height` on all 15 samples). What is NEW is `panelBottom`, which no prior sample carried: the viewport collapses to 424 while the PANEL keeps its full pre-keyboard extent, so the composer is held up only by `position: sticky` against a viewport that has shrunk out from under a panel that has not. ⛔ **NOT FIXED IN THIS FLIGHT — Russ's instruction, recorded so nobody reads the measurement as a fix.** ▶ The next question this makes answerable and did not before: is 1,563 ≈ the pre-keyboard panel height minus the post-keyboard viewport, i.e. does the panel simply never re-measure? That is one more screenshot, not a build. src: measurement 2026-08-07.
- ★CHAT-PROBE-DISPLAY-CANNOT-SHOW-DISMISSAL — ⚙ **CORRECTED 2026-08-05 BY THE PROBE RUN ITSELF, AND ONE HALF OF WHAT I BANKED THIS MORNING WAS WRONG.** I wrote that the freeze latch blocks the after-dismissal sample. **IT DOES NOT, BECAUSE IT NEVER ENGAGES:** the latch fires only when `doc.clientHeight − vv.height > 100`, and that difference was **0 on all 15 samples** — so `keyboardUp` is never true, `frozenRef` never latches, and the display live-updates forever. **THAT is why Russ saw two different `panelBottom` values seconds apart.** ⛔ The banked claim was a mechanism asserted from a code read and falsified by the first measurement — LORAMER_ESSENCE_LAW_9, my own, same day. **WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS THE REAL DEFECT: the rendered line still NEVER prints `offsetTop`**, the field the whole diagnosis turned on, so the screen could not answer the question at any point. **AND A SECOND, NEWLY MEASURED ONE: `panelBottom` IS MEANINGLESS ON THIS SURFACE.** `panelRef` is the shelf's fixed-height `.panel` but the PAGE's whole-document root, so the reported bottom is `rootHeight − scrollY` — verified EXACT on all 15 samples (10112−515=9597, 10323−9560=763). Russ's 763 and 9597 are both CORRECT and are a scroll-position readout wearing a geometry label. **ONE SHARED PROBE, TWO SURFACES, ONE FIELD THAT MEANS DIFFERENT THINGS — the same class as [[★CHAT-GUARD-CONTAINER-MOUNT-UNASSERTED]].** ORIGINAL ENTRY BELOW. **NEW 2026-08-05. THE INSTRUMENT ALREADY CAPTURES THE ANSWER AND THE SCREEN STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SHOW IT.** `LORAMER_NEXT_CHAT_VIEWPORT_PROBE_V1` is live in production: `?debug=chat` (sticky in sessionStorage), every sample POSTs to `/api/debug/viewport-probe`, which logs one `LORAMER_VIEWPORT_PROBE` line server-side carrying **`vv.offsetTop`, `vv.height`, `doc.clientHeight`, scale and phase**. ⛔ **SO THE SERVER HAS EVERYTHING NEEDED AND NO DEPLOY IS REQUIRED.** **WHAT THE SCREEN CANNOT DO, and both halves matter:** (a) the rendered line prints `scale · vvH · docH · overhang · panelBottom` and **NEVER `offsetTop`** — the one field the open diagnosis turns on; (b) `LORAMER_NEXT_CHAT_PROBE_FREEZE_V1` latches `frozenRef` on the FIRST keyboard-up sample and never calls `setProbeLine` again, and on the Lora page `active` is permanently `true` so the latch never resets — **therefore the AFTER-DISMISSAL sample can never be displayed.** That freeze was a correct fix for a real defect (a live-updating readout produced a true number from the wrong phase) and it is now the exact thing blocking the next measurement. ⚠ **`--lora-kb-inset` IS NOT IN THE PAYLOAD, but it is EXACTLY DERIVABLE** from the three captured numbers via the code's own formula (`raw = docH - offsetTop - vvH; inset = raw > 100 ? raw : 0`) — derived, never measured, and it must be labelled as such wherever it is quoted. ⛔ **RETENTION IS THE REAL LIMIT:** Vercel runtime logs expire quickly, so a probe run must be READ soon after it is taken. ▶ TO CLOSE: either render `offsetTop` and keep a per-phase row (before / keyboard-up / after-dismissal) instead of one frozen line, or accept the server as the read path permanently. src: 2026-08-05 recon. open

BOTH HALVES SHIPPED, WHICH IS THE ONLY WAY THIS ITEM COULD EVER HAVE CLOSED — LORAMER_CHAT_COPY_BLOCKS_V1 (the button) + LORAMER_CHAT_PASTE_ABLE_OUTPUT_V1 (the fence it attaches to). DECISIONS owns both settled records; not restated here.** The entry's own warning — "Build the button alone and it will look shipped and be useless on the exact answers it exists for" — was the reason the brief was stopped and re-scoped BEFORE any code was written, and it is the reason Flight A deliberately did not close this. ⛔ **THE PROMPT HALF'S REQUIREMENT IS THE FENCE'S CONTENTS, NOT THE FENCE:** raw lines only, one value per line, no numbering, bullets, quotes, header row, or commentary/metrics inside — because a fenced block of `1. running shoes` COPIES CLEANLY AND THEN FAILS ON PASTE, which looks like the feature worked and is strictly worse than no fence. It runs later as a baseline check, not as that flight's gate. ⚠ **AND THE GUARD'S LIMIT IS ON THE RECORD: `paste-able-output.guard.mjs` proves the instruction is PRESENT, REACHABLE and in the CACHED PREFIX — it cannot prove Lora OBEYS it.** A green run means the rule exists, never that the output is right. ORIGINAL ENTRY BELOW. ⚙ **FLIGHT A (THE BUTTON) SHIPPED 2026-08-06 as LORAMER_CHAT_COPY_BLOCKS_V1 — DECISIONS owns the settled record and it is not restated here.** What landed: a `components={{ pre: … }}` override on the -next markdown path, working MID-STREAM by construction (an unterminated fence is already a `<pre>`), with both markdown call sites — completed turn AND streaming preview — collapsed onto ONE `<Md>` renderer so the override cannot be present on one and absent on the other. The copied flag is reset-keyed on clientId ([[d55f739]] one layer down: the shelf stays mounted across a client switch and `messages.map` keys by index), the button node is excluded from the copy by identity so "Copy" can never be pasted into a negative-keyword box, and a clipboard rejection leaves the flag FALSE rather than claiming success. Guarded by `tests/guards/chat-copy-blocks.guard.mjs` (7 legs, seen RED at 14 findings against pre-fix HEAD on a throwaway copy), which also pins the -next-only blast radius structurally — legacy `/dashboard` imports neither the component nor its stylesheet. ⚠ **TWO THINGS WORTH CARRYING:** `scripts/run-guards.mjs` is an EXPLICIT LIST, not a directory scan — a new guard file does nothing until it is added there, and mine did not run until I noticed the total had not moved; and `.md pre` gained `position: relative` (a change to a SHIPPED rule) because the button sits inside the `<pre>` and would otherwise have escaped to the portaled panel. ⛔ **STILL OWED — FLIGHT B:** the prompt instruction that makes Lora emit paste-able answers as FENCED RAW LINES (no numbering, no bullets, no header row), which is the half without which the button is decorative. ORIGINAL ENTRY BELOW. **PROMOTED 2026-08-05 from prose inside RANKED ORDER #6(d) to its own entry, so a grep finds it.** Recorded rank: #6(d), precondition (5b streaming) MET. - ★CHAT-DESKTOP-SIDE-PANEL — **PROMOTED 2026-08-06 from prose inside RANKED ORDER #6(j), and EXTENDED with the first direct observation of the reference product. THIS IS THE ONE HOME FOR SIDEKICK FINDINGS — [[★CHAT-UPLOAD-IN-COMPOSER]], [[★CHAT-THREAD-IDENTITY]] and [[★CHAT-STOP-BUTTON]] point here rather than each keeping a copy.** ORIGINAL SCOPE, unchanged: chat as a SIBLING panel that SHRINKS the dashboard, not an overlay that covers it; four controls (preview, expand-to-full, collapse, close); expand/collapse state STICKY PER USER; the panel width becomes a real dashboard BREAKPOINT so GRID-NATIVE law applies — the grid reflows into the narrower width, it does not get occluded. ⛔ **OBSERVED 2026-08-06 ~00:26Z, FOUR SCREENS OF SHOPIFY SIDEKICK ON `admin.shopify.com` IN CHROME ON iOS — AND THE BROWSER IS WHY IT COUNTS.** A native-app comparison can always be dismissed as "they have capabilities we do not"; this was WEB, IN A MOBILE BROWSER, under the same viewport, keyboard-inset and no-native-chrome constraints [[LORAMER_GATE_B_TARGET_IS_CHROME_IOS_V1]] that produced every composer defect this repo has fixed. It is therefore an EXISTENCE PROOF, not an aspiration. **WHAT WAS SEEN, and each line is a design question we currently answer differently or not at all:** **(1) COMPOSER** — a single rounded field with "+" and voice INLINE INSIDE the field at the right, and NO separate send button until there is text. The affordance count at rest is lower than ours and the send button earns its space instead of occupying it empty. **(2) ATTACH SHEET** — Camera and Files as two large tiles, THEN domain shortcuts (Products, Orders, Customers, Collections) and Skills / Apps. ⇒ **THE FRAMING IS "WHAT CAN I BRING INTO THIS CONVERSATION", NOT "ATTACH A FILE"**, and that is the transferable idea: our equivalent of their Products/Orders/Customers is clients, campaigns, date ranges and saved views, none of which is reachable from the composer today. **(3) SETTINGS** — ONE line: Memory, a toggle, a plain-language explanation. Against our `/api/memory` layer that is a whole surface we have never designed and could ship as one row. **(4) HISTORY** — its own FULL SCREEN, searchable, grouped by time, tappable to resume. Not a dropdown, not a menu. **(5) SHELL** — full-height panel with its own header and a conversation-name switcher in the title. ⛔ **DOES SIDEKICK ALREADY ANSWER THE DESIGN QUESTION? PER ITEM, HONESTLY, AND NOTHING IS RE-RANKED BY THIS ENTRY:** vs [[★CHAT-UPLOAD-IN-COMPOSER]] — **PARTLY.** It confirms the "+"-inside-the-field placement and validates splitting the affordance from the file type, but Sidekick's sheet leads with CAMERA, which is precisely the IMAGE half Russ has deferred; it answers the PLACEMENT question and not the SCOPE question. vs [[★CHAT-THREAD-IDENTITY]] — **YES, AND IT RAISES THE COST OF NOT DOING IT.** A searchable, time-grouped, tappable history screen and a conversation-name switcher are both IMPOSSIBLE on our schema: `client_conversations` has no thread id, so "a conversation" is only a `(client_id, user_email, surface, created_at)` tuple. Sidekick shows what the missing id buys. vs [[★CHAT-STOP-BUTTON]] — **NO. NOT OBSERVED.** No stop control appeared in any of the four screens, and absence in four screenshots is not evidence about the product. ⛔ Do not cite Sidekick for or against the stop button; our requirement (must CANCEL SERVER-SIDE, not hide output) stands on its own billing argument. vs THIS ENTRY'S OWN DESKTOP PANEL — **NOT ANSWERED. WRONG SCREEN.** All four observations are the MOBILE FULL-HEIGHT presentation; the desktop shrink-vs-overlay question is untouched and still needs its own look. ⚠ **WHAT THIS IS NOT: a ranking change.** It is a reference set. Rank #6(j), and the ★CHAT-UI-DEDICATED-DAY items keep the order they had. src: banked 2026-07-27, promoted + extended 2026-08-06 from four device screenshots. open
- ★EVAL-COST-PER-CORRECT-ANSWER — **NEW 2026-08-06. AN EVAL REQUIREMENT, NOT A COST-CONTROL ITEM, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ENTRY.** ⛔ **THE REQUIREMENT: the 100-question eval must score BOTH quality AND cost per correct answer, and must never report one without the other.** Russ raised it from a Stanford agent-memory finding whose transferable claim is that **two systems with IDENTICAL accuracy can differ enormously in cost, and accuracy alone hides that completely** — an accuracy-only scorecard cannot distinguish a system that is right cheaply from one that is right expensively, and by 9/30 that difference is the product. ⚠ **VERIFIED FROM SOURCE RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because "the ledger already exists" is exactly the shape of claim this repo has been burned by five times ([[LORAMER_ESSENCE_LAW_9_V1]]):** `tests/lora-evals/spend-ledger.mjs` (LORAMER_EVAL_SPEND_LEDGER_V1) DOES record **per-question** chat and judge spend and **refuses to print a total it could not measure** — its own words, `⛔ CHAT SPEND NOT MEASURED — this run CANNOT report what it cost`. **SO THE PRIMITIVE IS REAL AND THE GAP IS NARROWER THAN "build cost tracking":** `run-evals.mjs` calls `ledger.report(rec)` as a SEPARATE SECTION from the scorecard, and **nothing joins spend to pass/fail.** ⇒ **THE ACTUAL WORK IS A JOIN AND A SECOND COLUMN: dollars ÷ CORRECT answers, alongside dollars ÷ questions asked.** ⛔ **AND THE DENOMINATOR IS THE TRAP:** cost-per-correct must divide by GRADED CORRECT answers only — [[★EVAL-HARNESS-SCORED-NO-ANSWER-AS-FAILURE]] already cost this project a scorecard that read 9/40 when the truth was 9/22, and a cost figure divided by the wrong denominator will be wrong in the *flattering* direction, which is worse. ⛔ **THE LAW THIS DOES NOT TOUCH, BANKED HERE SO NOBODY REOPENS IT: the source argues for "ENGINEERING FORGETTING", AND THAT IS ABOUT THE CONTEXT LAYER, NOT THE STORE.** What is curated is WHAT REACHES THE MODEL PER QUESTION — the prompt, the retrieved slice, the conversation window. **EVERY ROW IS STILL KEPT FOREVER.** Deleting captured rows to reduce cost would destroy the asset the whole platform is ([[LORAMER_GEO_RESOLVER_V1]]'s NEVER DELETE A ROW is the same principle applied to reference data) and would make history unrecoverable at the vendor retention wall, which no token saving can buy back. **Curate the feed; keep the store.** ⚠ AND NOTE THE TENSION WITH [[★LORA-ONE-REGISTER]] rather than pretending they are one item: cost-per-correct rewards the SHORT path, the register item warns that thoroughness is what produced the refund caveat nobody asked for. A cost column that is read without the quality column will quietly argue for a worse product — which is precisely why the requirement is BOTH, never one. Cross-ref [[★EVAL-SET-EXPANSION]] (the 100-question set this lands in), [[★TWO-EVAL-HARNESSES-ONE-JUDGE]] (two harnesses, only one can judge — the column has to land in whichever survives), [[★USAGE-CAP-ABSENT]] (no cap anywhere; at $0 balance Lora BLANKS). src: Russ 2026-08-06, Stanford agent-memory finding. open

(2) `lora-back-parity` used `router\.push\(fallback\)` in BOTH its locator and leg (e) — the exact call with exactly no arguments — so `{ scroll: false }` read as "the fallback is gone". (3) `landing-scroll`'s own first run flagged correct code because a `{/*` JSX comment quoting `router.back()` was not stripped by a line-prefix test. ▶ **THE RULE THAT FALLS OUT: ANCHOR ON THE CALLEE, NEVER ON THE FULL ARGUMENT LIST**, and strip block comments span-wise before matching. ⛔ **THE REAL WORK IS AN AUDIT: how many of the 74 guards locate by a literal that a legitimate edit would move? UNKNOWN, and unknowable without reading each.** ⚠ Related and compounding: [[★GUARD-IGNORES-LORAMER-GUARD-ROOT]] — a guard that also ignores the root override cannot even be RED-proved safely. src: 2026-08-07, third occurrence. open ⛔ **BLAST RADIUS: UNKNOWN — SAME REASONING AS [[★GUARD-IGNORES-LORAMER-GUARD-ROOT]] AND THEY COMPOUND.** A locator that pins today's literal turns a CORRECT edit into a structural RED ("cannot locate", "the fallback is gone"), and the honest reading of that red — "my change broke something" — is wrong, so the pressure is to contort the CODE to satisfy the matcher. **A guard that ignores LORAMER_GUARD_ROOT cannot even be RED-proved safely, so the two together mean a guard can be both un-provable and spuriously red.** ▶ **RANKED AHEAD OF FURTHER CHAT-UI POLISH 2026-08-07, with the root-override audit, as one piece of work: read all 74 guards for BOTH defects at once.** UNSCOPED.
- ★LANDING-PROBE-SPEC-IS-WRONG — ⛔ **NEW 2026-08-07. TWO DEFECTS, BOTH MINE, IN THE INSTRUMENT SHIPPED BY LORAMER_NEXT_LANDING_PROBE_VISIBLE_V1 (1602e63).** **(a) MISMATCHED BASES.** `sH` is `document.documentElement.scrollHeight`; `vp` is `window.innerHeight`. **"No overflow" is `scrollHeight === documentElement.clientHeight`, and the readout never prints `clientHeight`.** On Chrome iOS those diverge — already banked as [[LORAMER_LAYOUT_VIEWPORT_TRACKS_VISUAL_ON_CHROME_IOS_V1]], where `documentElement.clientHeight` tracks `visualViewport.height` (763→424 across 15 samples). ⇒ **THE PROBE COMPARES TWO DIFFERENT OBJECTS AND CANNOT ESTABLISH THE THING IT WAS BUILT TO ESTABLISH.** **(b) THE ARMING WINDOW CLOSES AT `ARRIVAL_GRACE_MS + 400` = 800ms** — before the thread hydrates, and before every ResizeObserver-driven `bottom()` that would show `scrollHeight` jumping to thousands. **The instrument stops watching before the interesting thing happens.** ⛔ **THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A NIT: while `sH == vp` the maximum scroll offset is ZERO, so TOP AND BOTTOM ARE THE SAME POSITION, and a reading of `y 0` CANNOT DISTINGUISH SUCCESS FROM FAILURE. In exactly the regime it was built to diagnose, it is blind by construction.** ⚠ **AND I TOLD RUSS IT WOULD DECIDE THE HEIGHT-RACE-vs-ROUTER FORK. IT CANNOT, AS BUILT — that claim was wrong when I made it.** ▶ **NEUTERED 2026-08-07, NOT DELETED**, and the reasoning is on the face of it: the VISIBILITY plumbing (on-screen readout, arming, per-landing reset, the render path) is correct and was the hard part; only the SPEC is wrong. The gate moved from `loramer:debug-chat` to **`loramer:debug-landing`, which nothing sets** — so it is INERT in production, Russ cannot meet it again through the flag he actually opens for the FRAME probe, and whoever repairs it can re-arm it by hand. Both defects are written into the file header at the gate. `router-scroll-off.guard.mjs` leg (f) now PINS the neutering. src: 2026-08-07. open

## I. LESSONS INDEX 1–60 (+ dated)  (source: LORAMER_DECISIONS.md)
1 Silent-skip via shared marker — use content-based idempotency, not marker-presence.
2 Scope assumption in destructure adds — grep the prop in the parent's scope before patching.
3 TS prop add = two edits/component (destructure AND type; check inline vs multi-line type).
4 JS string apostrophes break builds — use backticks for any string with apostrophes/quotes.
5 Stale anchors — re-read the current file (fresh sed/grep) before any patch.
6 Marker-collision silent failure — distinct sub-markers OR per-edit content checks.
7 Per-edit content-based idempotency check is the best practice (all/some/none present logic).
8 Silent .catch(()=>[]) hides GAQL/API errors — instrument console.error before concluding "no data".
9 Cache invalidation hides deployed fixes (15-min) — force a miss via a never-used date range.
10 Whitespace in anchors — bytes matter; dump exact bytes when an anchor fails.
11 PROMPT-AS-MIRROR — grounding/constraint text goes in code comments (INTERNAL_GROUNDING), never user-rendered prompt.
12 Meta breakdowns go in &breakdowns=, NOT &fields= (else HTTP 400, swallowed by .catch).
13 Same-line comment after a token (comma/paren/bracket/template) can break webpack — comment on its own line.
14 tsc --noEmit is NOT npm run build — webpack is stricter (syntax/mangled-literals); build is the real gate.
15 Surfacing raw API status/body into the prompt = diagnostic of last resort (always with a planned cleanup).
16 Anchor only from the current-turn paste — never memory/earlier turns/grep; small anchors over big.
17 Same-named files + blind mv is dangerous — unique-name downloads before moving.
18 Patch scripts with hardcoded machine paths silently fail — match the machine's path.
19 ONE canonical date resolver (resolveDateWindow) — never roll per-platform date math.
20 Revenue = NET (currentSubtotalPriceSet), not gross — surface refunds; match merchant analytics.
21 GAQL has NO LAST_90_DAYS enum — explicit BETWEEN via resolveDateWindow.
22 Platform selector and tab nav are separate controls — switch to Overview on platform change from a non-ad tab.
23 Safe Supabase dup cleanup — backup→repoint children→verify counts→delete only emptied twins (keeper isn't always older).
24 Bug hunts in big files — investigate-only first, then a tight fix spec.
25 Repo is single source of truth — git pull at session start on either machine; unpushed work doesn't travel.
26a Serverless backfill cross-request cursor race — do the whole job in ONE invocation (in-memory loop); persist the cursor only for resume-after-interrupt, never as the loop's control.
26b RightPanel renders TWIN desktop/mobile message containers (hidden md:flex / flex md:hidden, both in DOM) — audit BOTH when touching either; assign anchors by document order. (HANDOFF dual-numbered both as "26"; HANDOFF:730 explicitly notes the collision.)
27 zsh eats unquoted globs (quote --include="*.ts"); BSD grep needs -E for alternation.
28 Verify a freshly-deployed cron/route against LIVE prod + give it time (stale triggers/logs mislead).
29 Heredoc/terminal pastes drop characters — deliver code as files; tsc catches mangled identifiers, NOT mangled string literals — grep critical strings.
30 Backfill depth = "as deep as the platform serves," discovered by probing; report the ACTUAL earliest row, never the swept cursor.
31 Per-platform retention differs — probe before trusting any documented limit.
32 JSX comments are {/* */}, not /* */ (renders as visible text; tsc misses it).
33 CRON-GATED VERIFICATION — deploy before the cron window or manually trigger after; capture writes YESTERDAY's date.
34 Handoffs anchor on session TAG + files, never a commit hash (local commits squash/rewrite on push).
35 pg_dump in CI: invoke by ABSOLUTE path /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/pg_dump (PATH resolves to v16).
36 GitHub Actions "Re-run jobs" replays the ORIGINAL commit — use a fresh workflow_dispatch to test a fix.
37 Vercel env rotation needs a redeploy to bind; native cron rotates atomically with the redeploy.
38 Supabase DB password is reset-safe (app uses API keys, not raw Postgres password).
39 A DB write that must touch a row → UPSERT (not UPDATE) + check affected count, log loudly on 0; never assume success on no-throw.
40 Never render internal flag/enum/status/tier keys to users — pass through a human-label map next to the keys.
41 Stripe Portal "cancel at period end" sets cancel_at (timestamp), not cancel_at_period_end (boolean).
42 Google OAuth consent-screen edits (name/domains/scopes/URLs/logo) trigger RE-verification — treat as frozen at launch.
43 Google Ads permissible-use update → Tool Change Form (zero-risk MCC metadata), not a full Standard Access app.
44 Walk every onboarding identity SHAPE with a real identity before launch (founder-only testing only exercises one shape).
45 vercel env pull can report a populated prod var as blank — verify "empty env" against runtime behavior; never re-set to a guess.
46 An API probe verifies what the CREDENTIAL can see, not what EXISTS — a boundary coinciding with a known limit IS the explanation; scope-truncated $0 rows are false-zeros, delete them.
47 EVERYTHING GETS EVERYTHING — completeness is a CORRECTNESS requirement; every gap explicit; any cap is a logged deliberate decision (MATRIX).
48 Vercel MCP has NO env-write — rotate via CLI (value via stdin, never printed) + redeploy to bind.
49 Guard NOT-NULL numerics vs NaN at the WRITE BOUNDARY (Number.isFinite), not per-builder (NaN ?? 0 = NaN → 23502 drops the whole row).
50 Don't conclude a logic bug from a symptom seen under one timing — replay the exact query against live DB; schedule catchup AFTER forward.
51 A backfill DRIVER LOOP must circuit-break on a persistent per-window error; never oscillate/re-walk; be gentle on live stores; resume from the TRUE frontier; when in doubt, STOP and surface.
52 Next.js App Router caches global fetch → deterministic supabase-js reads/writes go STALE/DROPPED on Vercel; force-no-store on read-after-write routes; a unique request body masks the bug.
53 A persisted UI selection carried across a context switch must be RE-VALIDATED against the new context (derive caps from the incoming entity); land on a valid non-blank default.
54 Shopify managed-install scopes come from the DEPLOYED config (shopify app deploy), not the authorize-URL scope= param; a refresh preserves the original grant; verify a scope change by PROBE.
55 A flag-gated reconnect control can be invisible exactly when needed — any re-auth/extend-scope affordance must be reachable for a HEALTHY connection.
56 shopify app deploy needs the Shopify CLI on node ≥22.12 (CLI 4.x crashes on node 20).
57 Vercel env VALUES are unreadable from tooling (masked / pull-blanked / no MCP env tool) — confirm from the source system.
58 Shopify revenue basis differs BY GRAIN — reconcile to the cent (per-line refund attribution + pro-rata residual) or ship a silent per-SKU lie; a WRONG basis is worse than no basis.
59 A permanent-history backfill must self-reconcile per unit of work (Σ within 1¢ each day BEFORE write/cursor-advance) or HALT loudly — never persist a bad day.
60 A connection-state claim (broken/dead/frozen/blocked/unhealthy/reconnect-needed) is a HYPOTHESIS until a LIVE capture-path probe proves it — never written as fact from a stored flag (health/last_error_code/oauth_190/last_ok_at) alone; stored flags are DERIVED CONTEXT, not ground truth (same class as the Google end_date adapter-semantics bug). Origin: a prior session wrote "Influential Drones Meta BLOCKED/broken/oauth_190" into CONTINUE_HERE + QUEUE + a session log as settled fact from the flag alone — it was FALSE (token alive HTTP 200, warehouse reconciled to the penny) and survived days because each session read it forward without re-deriving. RULE: before writing any negative connection claim into ANY handoff doc, run a live probe (raw HTTP status + body, Lesson 15 style); until probed, record "flag says X — UNVERIFIED, probe before acting," never as a blocker. The transient-190-dark-flags-a-live-connection generator = WS2 #2 (separate fix).
61 A backfill writer must STOP AT its retention floor as an EMPTY SUCCESS (per-adapter granularMonths clamp — meta=36, GA fixed 2015-08-14, Google account/dim 132mo), NOT overshoot into a boundary THROW; a step is 'done' ONLY on empty-success-at-floor or reconciled-to-floor, NEVER on an error. Origin: the onboarding drain's Meta account step stoppedOnError at the ~37mo boundary (it overshot to 132mo), never completed, and BLOCKED the later placement step. Fix (LORAMER_ONBOARD_DRAIN_V1): granularMonths=36 for meta; PER-STEP-INDEPENDENT drain (a stuck early step never starves a later one); verified Meta taxonomy decides done-vs-retry-vs-surface ({1,2,4,17,613,80004}/429/timeout=retry · 100·1487534=narrow-the-window · 100-other/190/368=surface · empty-success=done); NEVER swallow the fetch error (L15) — surface code/subcode so floor-vs-transient is distinguishable.
62 A platform-wide "stall" + a cluster of serverless TIMEOUTS with NO DB/lock/deadlock evidence and NO code-deploy correlation = look UPSTREAM at the external API's QUOTA, not infra. The 2026-06-28 Google 504 cluster (06:20–11:40Z) AND the 4h geo "stall" were ONE event: Basic-Access developer-scope quota exhaustion (15k ops/day, one shared dev token) burned by the morning geo fan-out by ~11:32Z. FALSIFIED, explicitly: (a) Supabase swap/memory and (b) BUDGET_MS 680 — neither caused nor fixed the 504s (they ran 5.5h AFTER the BUDGET_MS deploy and stopped exactly when geo WRITES stopped, 3.5h BEFORE the Supabase resize). Read the REAL error bytes (e.errors[0]) before blaming infra; correlate the symptom's start/stop against the actual workload, not against whatever was deployed.
63 A backfill lap that throws OR fails to advance but lets the cron fire return HTTP 200 is a SILENT failure — geo was DEAD 4h under green 200s with the error masked as "[object Object]". Every drain fire must return ok:false/failed:N + console.error for ANY thrown/non-200 lap (ALL platforms); a dead/non-advancing lap can never read as a green fire. (LORAMER_GOOGLE_QUOTA_GUARD_V1 CHANGE 1.)
64 TWO completion authorities that can disagree are a stall trap: the sync_state cursor backfill_complete (writer) vs platform_connections.onboard_steps_done (drain). A stale done-flag over an INCOMPLETE cursor silently SKIPS a client forever (Woo Shelley: onboard ['woo'] done but cursor complete=false at 2018-12-13, owes to ~2015 — frozen ~12d; drain pending filter excludes her). The cursor must be the SINGLE completion authority; any path that re-opens a cursor to complete=false MUST clear that step key from onboard_steps_done.
65 Woo backfill "complete = one 21-day all-status-ZERO chunk" (woocommerce-backfill.ts) can FALSE-complete on any >21-day sales GAP mid-history — a quiet store stretch reads as history-start. When hardening woo completeness: probe the store's true oldest order, or require N consecutive zero chunks.
66 supabase-js .upsert(row) WITHOUT an explicit { onConflict } defaults its conflict target to the PRIMARY KEY. On a table whose real dedup key is a SECONDARY UNIQUE column (meta_tokens: PK=id + UNIQUE(user_email)), and where the PK is auto-generated (no id in the row), the upsert becomes an INSERT → it violates the secondary UNIQUE → 409, and if the returned error is discarded the write is a SILENT no-op that still looks successful. This bit the Meta callback: re-auth never rewrote the token (only the first-ever connect worked; the success redirect fired regardless), which broke the cote@ refresh. RULE: every upsert names its conflict target explicitly ({ onConflict: '<the-unique-column>' }) AND checks the returned error (fail loud — redirect/throw, never swallow, per L15). Gate-A a token/dedup upsert by reproducing the SECOND write to an existing key: buggy path 409s, fixed path UPDATES in place (id stable, 1 row). (LORAMER_META_CALLBACK_ONCONFLICT_V1, 2026-07-02.)
67 A Gate-A that checks only STATUS CODES can pass while the BEHAVIOR is broken — assert the behavior the gate exists to protect, not just 2xx/3xx. Origin: the 138a820 legacy-surface middleware silently broke the signup funnel two ways and that flight's Gate-A missed BOTH because it only read status codes: (a) it gated /agency + /business — the PRE-AUTH two-door signup pages — so unauthenticated new users were bounced to /login (the pages' content was never read → public marketing doors misclassified as "legacy tenant pages"); (b) it redirected /dashboard → -next BEFORE the /dashboard layout's enforceWelcomeGate could fire, so a fresh user reached the empty -next portfolio with NO account_type (Add-client 409s). The Gate-A even OBSERVED break (b) — /dashboard-next/clients returned 200 for a brand-new no-account_type user — and read it as "not over-blocked" instead of "onboarding didn't fire." RULE: for any gate/redirect/auth change, (1) READ what each matched path actually IS before gating it (public vs authed, data vs marketing), and (2) assert the POSITIVE behavior it must preserve — "a fresh user is REDIRECTED to /welcome", "the door RENDERS unauthenticated" — a bare 200 or 307 is necessary, NEVER sufficient. (LORAMER_SIGNUP_FUNNEL_FIX_V1, 2026-07-14.)
(2026-06-22) Product/line grain must reconcile to its account grain on the SAME revenue basis; re-capture history ONLY AFTER the basis fix ships (re-capturing before forces a second pass — violates "never twice").
